*The thirteenth sūkta.*

## Sūkta 13 (Maṇḍala 2)

**Introduction to the sūkta (Sanskrit, transcribed)**

> ऋतुर्जनित्रीति त्रयोदशर्चं द्वितीयं सूक्तं गार्त्समदं । ऋतुः सप्तो-
> नांत्या त्रिष्टुबित्यनुक्रमणिका । अस्मभ्यं तद्वसो इति त्रयोदशी त्रिष्टुप् । शिष्टास्त्रि-
> ष्टु बंतपरिभाषया जगत्यः । इंद्रो देवता ॥ उक्थे तृतीयसवनेच्छावाकशस्त्रेऽस
> सूक्तस्य विनियोगः । सूत्रितं च । ऋतुर्जनित्री नू मर्तो भवा मित्रः । आ- ६-१ ।
> इति ॥ दशरात्रे षष्ठेऽहन्यपि तृतीयसवनेच्छावाकशस्त्र एतत्तूक्तं । ऋतुर्जनित्रीति
> नित्यान्यैकाहिकानि । आ. ८-४ । इति सूत्रितं ॥

> *ṛturjanitrīti trayodaśarcaṃ dvitīyaṃ sūktaṃ gārtsamadaṃ | ṛtuḥ sapto-*
> *nāṃtyā triṣṭubityanukramaṇikā | asmabhyaṃ tadvaso iti trayodaśī triṣṭup | śiṣṭāstri-*
> *ṣṭu baṃtaparibhāṣayā jagatyaḥ | iṃdro devatā ‖ ukthe tṛtīyasavanecchāvākaśastre 'sa*
> *sūktasya viniyogaḥ | sūtritaṃ ca | ṛturjanitrī nū marto bhavā mitraḥ | ā- 6-1 |*
> *iti ‖ daśarātre ṣaṣṭhe 'hanyapi tṛtīyasavanecchāvākaśastra etattūktaṃ | ṛturjanitrīti*
> *nityānyaikāhikāni | ā. 8-4 | iti sūtritaṃ ‖*

*Gist:* The thirteenth sūkta, ऋतुर्जनित्री (*ṛturjanitrī*), thirteen Ṛks, is the second sūkta of the second anuvāka; seer Gṛtsamada; the first twelve Ṛks are Jagatī, the last Triṣṭubh; deity Indra. It is used in the Acchāvāka's śastra at the third pressing of the Ukthya rite and on the sixth day of the Daśarātra, as prescribed in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra (6-1; 8-4).

**Anuvāda (Kannada)**

Translation—This sūkta beginning ऋतुर्जनित्री (*ṛturjanitrī*) is the second sūkta in the second anuvāka. It has thirteen Ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is Gṛtsamada. Since the Anukramaṇikā says ऋतुः सप्तोनांत्या त्रिष्टुप् (*ṛtuḥ saptonāṃtyā triṣṭup*), the last Ṛk, the thirteenth, beginning अस्मभ्यं तद्वसो (*asmabhyaṃ tadvaso*), is in the Triṣṭubh metre; the remaining twelve Ṛks are in the Jagatī metre; the deity is Indra. This sūkta is applied to the śastra mantras to be recited by the priest called Acchāvāka at the third pressing in the Ukthya sacrifice, as set out in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra by the sūtra ऋतुर्जनित्री नू मर्तो भवा मित्रः (*ṛturjanitrī nū marto bhavā mitraḥ*) (6-1); and it is set out by the sūtra ऋतुर्जनित्री नित्यानैकाहिकानि (*ṛturjanitrī nityānaikāhikāni*) (8-4) that this sūkta is to be recited among the śastra mantras recited by the Acchāvāka priest at the third pressing on the sixth day of the sacrifice called Daśarātra.

### Printed p. 684

*Running head: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā; Maṇḍala 2, Adhyāya 2, Sūkta 13; p. 684.*

**Heading of the sūkta (as supplied)**

Om. Sūkta 13. Maṇḍala 2, Anuvāka 2, Sūkta 13. Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 6, Varga 10, 11, 12. Number of ṛks in the sūkta: 13. Seer: Gṛtsamada. Deity: Indra. Metre: 1-12 Jagatī; 13 Triṣṭubh.

#### Ṛk 1

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> ऋ॒तुर्जनि॑त्री॒ तस्या॑ अ॒पस्परि॑ म॒क्षू जा॒त आवि॑श॒द्यासु॒ वर्ध॑ते ।
> तदा॑ह॒ना अ॑भवत्प्॒युषी॒ पयों॒शोः पी॒यूषं॑ प्रथ॒मं तदु॒क्थ्यं॑

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> ऋतुः । जनित्री । तस्याः । अपः । परि । मक्षु । जातः । आ । अविशत् । यासु । वर्धते ।
> तत् । अहनाः । अभवत् । पिप्युषी । पयः । अंशोः । पीयुषं । प्रथमं । तत् ।
> उक्तं ॥ १ ॥

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> ऋतुर्वर्षाख्यः कालो जनित्री सोमस्य जनयित्री जननी भवति । तस्याः परि
> तस्या जनन्याः सकाशाज्ञातः सोमोऽप उदकानि मक्षु शीघ्रमाविशत् । यास्वप्सु
> सोमो वर्धते ता अविशदित्यन्वयः । तस्मादप्पु प्रविष्टत्वात् सोम आहना आहंत-
> व्योऽभिषोतव्यो भवति । आहना इति सकारांतमिदं पदं । तथा च मंत्रवर्णः ।
> ये ते मदा आहनसो विहायसः । ९-७५-५ । इति । या चांशुरूपा सोमलता
> पयः सारभूतं पिप्युषी वर्धयंत्यभवत् ॥ प्यायतेर्लिटि क्वसौ लड्यजोश्चेति
> पीभावः । वसोः संप्रसारणं । उगितश्चेति जिप् ॥ अंशोस्तस्याः सोमलतायाः
> पीयूषं रसभूतं पय उक्थं प्रशस्यं हविरिंद्रस्य भवति ॥

*Gist:* The season (the rainy season) is the mother of Soma; Soma, born of her, quickly entered the waters in which he grows; hence he is to be pressed. The plant's milk, the essence, is the offering for Indra.

### Printed p. 685

*Running head: [Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 6, Varga 10] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā; p. 685.*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

ऋतुः (*ṛtuḥ*) — the rainy season. जनित्री (*janitrī*) — is the mother of Soma (the time that produces it). तस्याः परि (*tasyāḥ pari*) — from that mother. जातः (*jātaḥ*) — the Soma that has been born. यासु (*yāsu*) — in which waters. वर्धते (*vardhate*) — it grows. अपः (*apaḥ*) — such waters. मक्षु (*makṣu*) — quickly. आ विशत् (*ā viśat*) — enters, and. तत् (*tat*) — it. आहनाः (*āhanāḥ*) — becomes fit for pressing (that same Soma plant). पयः (*payaḥ*) — as the essence. पिप्युषी (*pipyuṣī*) — as the one that grows. अभवत् (*abhavat*) — becomes. अंशोः (*aṃśoḥ*) — of that same Soma plant. पीयूषं (*pīyūṣaṃ*) — the one that is the essence. प्रथमं (*prathamaṃ*) — the one that is chief. तत् (*tat*) — that juice. उक्थ्यं (*ukthyaṃ*) — becomes worthy of praise.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

The season called Varṣā (the rains) is the mother of Soma. The Soma born of that mother quickly enters the waters in which it grows. And, becoming the essence and the one that grows, it becomes fit for pressing. The juice of that same Soma plant, which is the essence and the chief, is worthy of praise.

**Printed English translation**

The season(of the rains) is the parent(of the Soma plant), which, as soon as born of her, enters into the waters in which it grows; thence it is fit for expression, as concentrating(the essence of the) water; and the juice of the Soma is especially to be praised(as the libation proper for Indra).

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

ऋतुर्जनित्री (*ṛturjanitrī*) — the rainy season, that is, the monsoon, is the mother of Soma. That is, just as other plants grow in the monsoon, the Soma plant also grows well and flourishes with the rain water. Therefore the seer describes the rainy season as the mother of Soma. Although this Ṛk has no word denoting the Soma plant, yet because the words अहनाः (*ahanāḥ*) पयः (*payaḥ*) अंशोः (*aṃśoḥ*), which help the explanation concerning the Soma juice, are present, and because the Ṛk too speaks of the pressing of Soma, the word सोमस्य (*somasya*) must be supplied by adhyāhāra so as to complete the sentence ऋतुः सोमस्य जनित्री (*ṛtuḥ somasya janitrī*).

तस्याः अपः परि मक्षु जातः आ अविशत् यासु वर्धते (*tasyāḥ apaḥ pari makṣu jātaḥ ā aviśat yāsu vardhate*) — Since the Soma plant that grows in that rainy season grows only by the support of water, "it entered the water" means that the plant filled with juice (water) and grew sturdy. This is the sense. Any plant, with the help of water in the rainy season, not only grows well but becomes moist, green and juicy. The Soma plant too, growing well in the rains and being full of juice — this juiciness of the plant the seer describes in another manner, as "growing in water and entering the water".

तत् आहनाः तस्मादप्पु प्रविष्टत्वात् सोम आहना आहंतवोऽभिषोतव्यो भवति । आहना इति सकारांतमिदं पदं । तथा च मंत्रवर्णाः । ये ते मदा आहनसो विहायसः (*tat āhanāḥ tasmādappu praviṣṭatvāt soma āhanā āhaṃtavo 'bhiṣotavyo bhavati | āhanā iti sakārāṃtamidaṃ padaṃ | tathā ca maṃtravarṇāḥ | ye te madā āhanaso vihāyasaḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-75-5) — Because the Soma plant is full of water (juice), it must be struck in order to bring that out, that is, it must be well beaten and crushed with stones. When it is so crushed, the juice comes out of the plant. This process is called आहनाः (*āhanāḥ*) or pressing. आहनाः (*āhanāḥ*) is a word ending in स (*sa*); the commentator says it is nominative singular. On this point he cites the Ṛk

ये ते मदा आहनसो विहायसस्तेभिरिंद्रं जोदय दातवे मघं (*ye te madā āhanaso vihāyasastebhiriṃdraṃ jodaya dātave maghaṃ*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-75-2)

and shows that the word आहनसः (*āhanasaḥ*) in it is a word ending in स (*sa*) and in the nominative plural.

अभवत् पिप्युषी पयः अंशोः पीयूषं प्रथमं तत् उक्ष्यं (*abhavat pipyuṣī payaḥ aṃśoḥ pīyūṣaṃ prathamaṃ tat ukṣyaṃ*) (as printed) — या चांशुरूपा सोमलता पयः सारभूतं पिप्युषी वर्धयंत्यभवत् । अंशोस्तस्याः सोमलतायाः पीयूषं रसभूतं पय उक्ष्यं प्रशस्यं हविरिंद्रस्य भवति (*yā cāṃśurūpā somalatā payaḥ sārabhūtaṃ pipyuṣī vardhayaṃtyabhavat | aṃśostasyāḥ somalatāyāḥ pīyūṣaṃ rasabhūtaṃ paya ukṣyaṃ praśasyaṃ haviriṃdrasya bhavati*) — On the word अंशु (*aṃśu*) Yāska says:

अंशुः शमष्टमात्रो भवति । अननाय शं भवतीति वा । (*aṃśuḥ śamaṣṭamātro bhavati | ananāya śaṃ bhavatīti vā |*)

(Si. 9-5, as supplied)

Since this Soma juice pervades the sacrificer (is spread in the sacrificer), that is, since the sacrificer drinks Soma, he becomes happy, thinking he has no sorrow or worry; since Soma pervades the sacrificer and produces happiness, Soma is called अंशु (*aṃśu*); or, since it produces happiness in the life of all beings (when Soma is drunk), it is called अंशु (*aṃśu*); or, since it gives happiness to those who have drunk Soma, Soma is called अंशु (*aṃśu*): so he has stated the etymology. From such a juicy Soma plant, its essential juice, the Soma juice, increases (by pressing). That is, by crushing with stones the Soma plants, which are moist, green and full of juice, and pressing out the juice, the Soma juice increases greatly, that is, is collected. The chief sense is that the Soma juice prepared in this way becomes an offering (food) praiseworthy, excellent or fit to be drunk, for Indra.

#### Ṛk 2

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> स॒ध्रीमा यं॑ति॒ परि॒ बिभ्र॑तीः॒ पयो॑ वि॒श्वप्स्न्या॑य॒ [?] प्र भ॑रंत॒ भोज॑नं ।
> स॒मा॒नो अध्वा॑ प्र॒वता॑मनु॒स्यदे॒ यस्ताकृ॑णोः प्रथ॒मं
> सास्यु॒क्थ्यः॑ ॥ २ ॥

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> सध्री । ईं । आ । यंति । परि । बिभ्रतीः । पयः । विश्वप्स्न्याय [?] । प्र । भरंत ।
> भोजनं ।
> समानः । अध्वा । प्रवतां । अनुस्यदे । यः । ता । अकृणोः । प्रथमं । सः । असि ।
> उक्थ्यः ॥ २ ॥

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> सध्री । अंचतेर्लुक् छांदसः । सहस्य सध्रिरिति सध्रादेशोऽंतोदात्तत्वेन
> निपातितः। सध्रीचीनाः पय उदकं परि परितो बिभ्रतीर्बिभ्राणा ईमेता नद्य आयंति।
> सर्वतो गच्छंति । ता नद्यो विश्वप्न्यास्यय विश्वासामपामाश्रयभूताय समुद्राय
> भोजनं ॥ भुज्यत इति भोजनं पयः ॥ प्रभरंत । प्रकर्षण संपादयंति । कुत
> एतत् तदाह । प्रवतां प्रवणवतां निम्मगानां पयसामनुष्यदे ॥ कृत्यार्थे तवै-
> केन्नेन्यत्वन इति केन्प्रत्ययः ॥ अनुष्यंदनीयोऽध्वा मार्गः समान एको हि ।
> यस्ता तानि सोमोत्पादननदीप्रवर्तनादीनि कर्माणि प्रथमं पूर्वमकृणोः ।
> अकरोः । स तादृङ्महिमोपेतस्त्वमुक्थोऽसि । सर्वैः प्रशस्यो भवसि ॥

*Gist:* The rivers, flowing together and bearing water, bring it as food to the sea, the support of all waters; the one path of flow is common, and Indra, who first did these deeds, is praised by all.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

सध्री (*sadhrī*) — flowing together. पयः (*payaḥ*) — water. परि (*pari*) — all around. बिभ्रतीः (*bibhratīḥ*) — bearing. ईं (*īṃ*) — these rivers. आ यंति (*ā yaṃti*) — spread and flow (and). विश्वप्स्याय (*viśvapsyāya*) — to the sea, the support of all waters. भोजनं (*bhojanaṃ*) — water. प्रभरंत (*prabharaṃta*) — fill completely. प्रवतां (*pravatāṃ*) — for the waters flowing to your region. अनुष्यदे (*anuṣyade*) — for flowing. अध्वा (*adhvā*) — the path. समानः (*samānaḥ*) — is of one form. यः (*yaḥ*) — who. ता (*tā*) — such

### Printed p. 688

*Running head: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā; Maṇḍala 2, Adhyāya 2, Sūkta 13; p. 688.*

(Pratipadārtha of Ṛk 2, continued:) प्रवाहानुकूलवाद कर्मगळन्नु (*pravāhānukūlavāda karmagaḷannu*) — the deeds favourable to the flow; प्रथमं (*prathamaṃ*) — first; अकृणोः (*akṛṇoḥ*) — you did; सः (*saḥ*) — such you, Indra; उक्त्यः असि (*uktyaḥ asi*) — you are worthy of praise (by all).

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

The rivers, flowing together and full of water, spread out and flow; and they fill with water the sea, the support of all waters. For the waters that flow to your region (the low ground) the path of flow is of one form. You, Indra, who first made such deeds favourable to the flow, are worthy of praise.

**Printed English**

The aggregated(streams) come, bearing everywhere the water, and conveying it as sustenance for the asylum of all rivers,(the ocean); the same path is(assigned) to all the descending(currents) to follow; and as he, who has(assigned) them(their course), you,(Indra), are especially to be praised.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

सध्री ईं आ यंति परि बिभ्रतीः पयॆः (*sadhrī īṃ ā yaṃti pari bibhratīḥ payèḥ*) — The rivers that flow in the rainy season carry in their broad beds the water that falls everywhere on the earth as rain. That is, all the rain water that falls on the earth comes and joins the rivers. In this way "all around" means the waters that come flowing and joining from their left and right; "bearing" means that the rivers hold them in their (river) beds and flow.

विश्वप्स्याय प्र भरंत भोजनं (*viśvapsyāya pra bharaṃta bhojanaṃ*) — The rivers bring and supply food to the sea, which is the support of all waters (the Sanskrit explanation of the words is quoted in the source). Where do the rivers that flow in this way go? All of them flow in order to bring water to the sea, the support of all waters, and fill it.

विश्वप्स्याय (*viśvapsyāya*) — to the sea, the support of all waters; the meaning is the sea, the support of the whole mass of water. If one says that the water that falls from the sky as rain and the water that flows in the river (being sweet) are different, so that this water does not rest on the sea, it is not so. Rain water and river water were at one time sea water itself. How? Sea water, heated by the sharp rays of the sun, is drawn up by the wind in the form of vapour and is transformed into clouds in the sky. From those clouds

### Printed p. 689

*Running head: [Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 6, Varga 10] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā; p. 689.*

rain arises, and that water falls on the earth, flows, and joins some river. If that river is a tributary flowing in your region, it joins a bigger river; if it is a big river it flows on by itself and finally reaches the sea. The final resting place of all rivers is the sea. Therefore the sea alone is said to be the support of the whole mass of water, whether on the earth or in the sky (in the form of clouds).

भोजनं—भुज्यत इति भोजनं पयः (*bhojanaṃ—bhujyata iti bhojanaṃ payaḥ*) — Whatever is eaten, a thing in the form of food, is called bhojana. Here the thing the sea needs is water. As the belly of animals or men is filled by food, so the sea is filled by water. "Water is the food of the sea" means that the waters the rivers bring and fill are in the form of food for the sea; that is, they are waters brought and poured in to fill it. The sentence विश्वप्न्यास्यय प्र भरंत भोजनं (*viśvapnyāsyaya pra bharaṃta bhojanaṃ*) used here by the Ṛṣi, with its words full of meaning and its sense full of feeling joined to a simile, displays the Ṛṣi's excellent skill of composition and his mastery of poetry.

समानः अध्वा प्रवतां अनुस्यदे यः ता अकृणोः प्रथमं सः असि उक्त्यः (*samānaḥ adhvā pravatāṃ anusyade yaḥ tā akṛṇoḥ prathamaṃ saḥ asi uktyaḥ*) — The path of the flowing water, or of the rivers, is the same; that is, since all the rivers flow in your regions, in the low ground, that low path is the path by which the rivers go and join the sea. The chief sense is: you, Indra, who first created (made) such a path, are worthy of praise. The Ṛṣi describes that Indra himself made the path by which the rain poured from the clouds falls on the earth, becomes rivers and flows to the sea, and that this immense work of Indra is praiseworthy.

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> विश्वा॒ एक॑स्य वि॒नुद॑स्तिक्षते॒ यस्ताकृ॑णोः प्रथ॒मं सास्यु॒त्थ्यः॑॥

> अनु । एकः । वदति । यत् । ददाति । तत् । रूपा । मिनन् । तत् अपाः । एकः ।
> ईयते ।

> *anu | ekaḥ | vadati | yat | dadāti | tat | rūpā | minan | tat apāḥ | ekaḥ |*
> *īyate |*

### Printed p. 690

*Running head: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā; Maṇḍala 2, Adhyāya 2, Sūkta 13; p. 690.*

> विश्वाः । एकस्य । विनुदः । ति ति क्षते । यः । ता । अकृणोः । प्रथमं । सः । असि ।
> उक्त्यः ॥ ३ ॥

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> यजमानो यद्धनिर्देवेभ्यो ददाति तदेको होतानुवदति । याज्या-
> पुरोनुवाक्याभ्यां देवताः स्मारयति । एकोऽध्वर्यू रूपा पश्वादीनां रूपाणि
> मिनन् हिंसन् तदपास्तद्विशसनाख्यमपः कर्म यस्य तादृशः सन् ईयते । देवय-
> जने सर्वत्र गच्छति । एकस्याध्वर्योर्विश्वा विनुदः सर्वाणि तत्कर्तृकाणि विक्षेपणरूपाणि
> कर्मवैगुण्यानि तितिक्षते । तद्योग्यप्रायश्चित्तकरणेन ब्रह्मा सहते ॥ गुप्तिज्ङ्भः सन्
> क्षमायामिष्यते ॥ तानि हविष्प्रदानादीनि कर्माणि यस्त्वमकृणोः । अकारयः सः
> त्वमुक्थोऽसि ॥

*Gist:* The sacrificer's offering is announced by the Hotṛ; the Adhvaryu moves about at the cutting of the victim; the Brahman priest repairs all ritual faults; you, Indra, who have had these rites performed, are praised.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

(यजमानः (*yajamānaḥ*) — the sacrificer.) यत् (*yat*) — the oblation that (he offers to the gods); ददाति (*dadāti*) — offers; तत् (*tat*) — that; एकः (*ekaḥ*) — one of the priests, the Hotṛ; अनुवदति (*anuvadati*) — announces (to the gods) with the yājyā and puronuvākyā verses. एकः (*ekaḥ*) — another, the Adhvaryu; रूपा (*rūpā*) — the limbs of the victim and the like; मिनन् (*minan*) — injuring (killing); तदपाः (*tadapāḥ*) — engaged in the work of cutting the limbs of the victim for the sacrificial offering; ईयते (*īyate*) — moves about. एकस्य (*ekasya*) — of the Adhvaryu; विश्वाः विनुदः (*viśvāḥ vinudaḥ*) — all the ritual faults; तितिक्षते (*titikṣate*) — (the priest in the form of Brahman) sets right by expiatory rites and the like; यः (*yaḥ*) — you who; ता अकृणोः (*tā akṛṇoḥ*) — have had all these rites performed and partaken of them; सः (*saḥ*) — such you; प्रथमं (*prathamaṃ*) — above all; उक्थः आसि (*ukthaḥ āsi*) — are worthy of praise.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

The oblation that the sacrificer offers to the gods is announced to the gods by the Hotṛ, one of the priests, with the yājyā and puronuvākyā verses. The other, the Adhvaryu, is engaged in the work of cutting up the victim and the like. All the ritual faults of these two are set right by the priest in the form of Brahman, by expiatory rites and the like. You, who have had all these rites performed and partaken of them, are praised above all.

**Printed English**

One(priest) announces(the offering) that he,(the institutor of the rite)
presents; another performs the act that apportions the limbs(of the victim);

### Printed p. 691

*Running head: [Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 6, Varga 10] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā; p. 691.*

a third corrects all the deficiencies of either, and as he, who has
enjoyed these(functions), you,(Indra), are especially to be praised.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

In this Ṛk the qualities of Indra are described: the functions that the priests (ṛtvij) such as the sacrificer, the Hotṛ and the Adhvaryu perform in the sacrifice are made to be done by Indra through each of them, and he is pleased.

अनु एकः वदति यत् ददाति (*anu ekaḥ vadati yat dadāti*) — यजमानो यद्धनिर्देवेभ्यो ददाति तदेको होतानुवदति । याज्यापुरोनुवाक्याभ्यां देवताः स्मारयति । (*yajamāno yaddhanirdevebhyo dadāti tadeko hotānuvadati | yājyāpuronuvākyābhyāṃ devatāḥ smārayati |*) When the sacrificer who performs the sacrifice offers to the gods the oblation, the ghee-offering and the like in the fire, he must do so reciting, appropriate to each time and each rite, mantras addressed to the deity. Such mantras are recited by the Hotṛ, one of the priests. First the Hotṛ recites the mantras called nivid, in praise of the qualities of the deity to whom the sacrificer offers the oblation. Then he recites the mantra called puronuvākyā, of the nature of praise or invitation to that deity, and invites the deity to come to the sacrificial ground. After the invitation, while the oblation is being offered in the fire to that deity, the Hotṛ recites the Ṛk called yājyā, whose sense is that the deity should accept the oblation. This same order is followed when an oblation is offered to every deity. Therefore, by the words यद्ददाति (*yaddadāti*) here is meant "whatever oblation the sacrificer offers", and by अन्वेको वदति (*anveko vadati*) that "in accordance with it, that is, mantras containing that very sense are recited by one (that is, by the Hotṛ, one of the priests)" is the main intention.

(अनु एकः यत् ददाति (*anu ekaḥ yat dadāti*)) तद्रूपा मिनन् तदपा एक ईयते—एकोऽध्वर्यू रूपा पश्वादीनां रूपाणि मिनन् हिंसन् तदपास्तद्विशसनाख्यमपः कर्म यस्य तादृशः सन् ईयते देवयजने सर्वत्र गच्छति । (*tadrūpā minan tadapā eka īyate—eko 'dhvaryū rūpā paśvādīnāṃ rūpāṇi minan hiṃsan tadapāstadviśasanākhyamapaḥ karma yasya tādṛśaḥ san īyate devayajane sarvatra gacchati |*) The commentator explains the sense thus: after the Hotṛ has recited the mantra suited to each time or each rite, the priest called Adhvaryu, engaged in the work of killing the victim, goes to and fro on the sacrificial ground, doing, according to rule, such acts as cutting up the limbs of the victim so that separate oblations can be made in the sacrificial offerings. Here a doubt arises. In this sentence the word अध्वर्यु (*adhvaryu*) is not used. And the words तद्रूपा मिनन्तदपाः (*tadrūpā minantadapāḥ*) yield the sense: injuring (that is, killing) the form of the victim and doing the acts connected with it, such as cutting the limbs. In the sacrifice neither killing the victim nor cutting its limbs is the work of the priest called Adhvaryu; for this work there is one called Śamitā. Since in the present

### Printed p. 692

*Running head: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā; Maṇḍala 2, Adhyāya 2, Sūkta 13; p. 692.*

Ṛk the word अध्वर्यु (*adhvaryu*) is absent, and the one who kills the victim is the Śamitā, the word एकः (*ekaḥ*) here may indicate the Śamitā himself. Or, since it is not impossible that in some circumstances the Adhvaryu performs the duties of other priests, the Adhvaryu may be what is suggested here. At any rate the meaning of the word एकः (*ekaḥ*) in this sentence remains one attended by doubt.

तद्रूपा मिनन् तदपाः (*tadrūpā minan tadapāḥ*) — Here Sāyaṇa explains the word तद्रूपा (*tadrūpā*) as the form (body) of the victim and the like, and तदपः (*tadapaḥ*) as तद्विशसनाख्यमपः (*tadviśasanākhyamapaḥ*), the rite of cutting it up. The word अपः (*apaḥ*) is read among the names of works (Nirukta 3-1). Although the word "victim" does not occur in this sentence, since the word मिनन् (*minan*) (injuring) is used, there is no objection to understanding तद्रूपा (*tadrūpā*) as the form of the victim.

विश्वाः एकस्य विनुधः तितिक्षते (*viśvāḥ ekasya vinudhaḥ titikṣate*) — एकस्याध्वयोर्विश्वा विनुधः सर्वाणि तत्कर्तृकाणि विक्षेपणरूपाणि कर्मवैगुण्यानि तितिक्षते । तद्योग्यप्रायश्चित्तकरणेन ब्रह्मा सहते (*ekasyādhvayorviśvā vinudhaḥ sarvāṇi tatkartṛkāṇi vikṣepaṇarūpāṇi karmavaiguṇyāni titikṣate | tadyogyaprāyaścittakaraṇena brahmā sahate*) When, through inadvertence in the sacrifice, deficiency or deviation arises in the various rites, the priest called Brahman sets them right by expiations and the like. That is the very work of the Brahman. Since the Adhvaryu has to do many kinds of work here (that is, in the sacrifice), it is not impossible that many lapses occur. The chief intention of this sentence is that the priest called Brahman sets right such acts, and the deficiencies that occur in the acts done by the other priests.

यः ता अकृणोः प्रथमं सः आसि उक्थ्यः (*yaḥ tā akṛṇoḥ prathamaṃ saḥ āsi ukthyaḥ*) — You, Indra, bring to completion by your inspiration the acts done by the three priests mentioned above. Therefore you, endowed with such a quality, are worthy of praise: thus Indra is praised.

#### Ṛk 4

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> असि॑न्व॒न्दंष्ट्रैः॑ पि॒तुर॑त्ति॒ भोज॑नं॒ यस्ताकृ॑णोः प्रथ॒मं सास्यु॒क्थ्यः॑ ॥ ४ ॥

> *prajābhyaḥ puṣṭiṃ vibhajaṃta āsate rayimina pṛṣṭhaṃ prabhavaṃtamāyate |*
> *asinvandaṃṣṭraiḥ pituratti bhojanaṃ yastākṛṇoḥ prathamaṃ sāsyukthyaḥ ‖ 4 ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> प्रजाभ्यः । पुष्टिं । विभजंतः । आसते । रयिंइव । पृष्ठं । प्रभवंतं आयते ।
> असिन्वन् । दंष्ट्रैः । पितुः । अत्ति । भोजनं । यः । ता । अकृणोः । प्रथमं । सः ।
> असि । उक्तैः ॥ ४ ॥

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> हे इंद्र पुष्टिं त्वया दत्तं पोषकं धनं स्वकीयाभ्यः प्रजाभ्यो विभजं-
> तोऽस्यॆतावदस्यॆतावदिति विभागं कुर्वंतो गृहमेधिन आसते । स्वस्वगृहेषु निव-
> संति । तत्र दृष्टांतः । आयते गृहं प्रत्यागच्छतेऽतिथये पृष्ठं धारकं प्रभवंतं
> बहुभरणसमर्थं रयिं धनं यथा विभज्य प्रयच्छंति तद्वत् । असिन्सन् सेतुबंधा-
> दिकं कर्म कुर्वन् लोकः पितुः पालयित्रा दिवः सकाशादागतं भोजनमुदकं
> तत्कार्या ओषधीर्दंष्ट्रैर्दंतैरत्ति । भक्षयति । यद्वा असिन्सन् अव्याप्रियमा-
> णोऽग्निः पितुः पालकस्य यजमानस्य संबंधि भोजनं हविर्लक्षणमन्नं दंष्ट्रै-
> र्दंतरूपैर्ज्वालैरत्ति । यस्ताकृणोरित्यादि सिद्धं ॥

*Gist:* Householders dwell in their houses, dividing the wealth you gave among their offspring as one shares wealth with a guest; creatures eat the water and plants; you, who made all this, are praised.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

आयते (*āyate*) — to the guest who comes to the house. पृष्ठं (*pṛṣṭhaṃ*) — sufficient. प्रभवंतं (*prabhavaṃtaṃ*) — fit to support many people. रयिं (*rayiṃ*) — as one shares out wealth. पुष्टिं (*puṣṭiṃ*) — nourishing (wealth given by you). प्रजाभ्यः (*prajābhyaḥ*) — to the offspring such as sons. विभजंतः (*vibhajaṃtaḥ*) — the sacrificers (householders) who divide and give. आसते (*āsate*) — dwell happily in their respective houses. असिन्वन् (*asinvan*) — doing works such as the building of dams. पितुः (*pituḥ*) — given by the protecting world of the gods. भोजनं (*bhojanaṃ*) — the water and the food created from it. दंष्ट्रैः (*daṃṣṭraiḥ*) — with the help of teeth. अत्ति (*atti*) — (the world) eats. यः (*yaḥ*) — you who. ता अकृणोः (*tā akṛṇoḥ*) — have caused all these acts to be done. सः (*saḥ*) — such you. प्रथमं (*prathamaṃ*) — very specially. उक्ष्यः असि (*ukṣyaḥ asi*) — are worthy of praise.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

Householders, the sacrificers who divide among their offspring such as sons the nourishing wealth given by you, as one shares out wealth sufficient for a guest who comes to the house and fit to support many people, dwell happily in their respective houses. Doing works such as the building of dams

### Printed p. 694

*Running head: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā; Maṇḍala 2, Adhyāya 2, Sūkta 13; p. 694.*

performing works, the world eats, with the help of its teeth, the water given by the protecting world of the gods and the food created from it. You who have caused all these acts to be done, such a one you are, very specially worthy of praise.

**Printed English**

Distributing nourishment to their progeny, they,(the householders), abide(in their dwellings), as if offering ample and sustaining wealth to a guest: constructing(useful works, a man) eats with his teeth the food(given him) by(his) protector, and as he, who has enjoined these(things to be done), you,(Indra), are especially to be praised.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

It is not clear what subject the Ṛṣi describes in this Ṛk. The commentator has fitted together one kind of meaning, but since the sense of some words is not clear, it cannot be said that the Ṛṣi's intention is just so.

प्रजाभ्यः पुष्टिं विभजंतः आसते (*prajābhyaḥ puṣṭiṃ vibhajaṃtaḥ āsate*) — The commentator's Sanskrit (हे इंद्र त्वया दत्तं पोषकं धनं (*he iṃdra tvayā dattaṃ poṣakaṃ dhanaṃ*) …, the bhāṣya passage continuing to गृहमेधिन (*gṛhamedhina*) आसते (*āsate*)) is followed in the Kannada by the explanation: "O Indra, the householders dwell, dividing the wealth you gave among their own offspring, saying 'this much to you, this much to you'." The householders, the masters of houses, divide the wealth you gave among those who depend on them, saying "this is for you, that is for him", and dwell happily in their respective houses. Wealth here may mean property, or food and the like. For the word पुष्टिं (*puṣṭiṃ*) indicates the sense of food and the like that produce nourishment in the body. The main intention is that the householders do not enjoy by themselves alone the things given by Indra, but divide them according to each one's need among their wives, sons, servants and the others who depend on them, enjoy a small part themselves, and live happily in their houses.

रयिमिव पृष्ठं प्रभवंतं आयते (*rayimiva pṛṣṭhaṃ prabhavaṃtaṃ āyate*) — In the sentence above an illustration has been given here about the householders' dividing of wealth. The commentator explains it in Sanskrit as: as they divide and give to a guest who comes to the house sufficient wealth, able to support many. That is, as the householders of a house receive a guest or visitor who has come to their house, honour him according to rule, and give him with a religious mind the food and wealth he needs, so, the illustration says, they divide among their dependants the wealth given by Indra. This illustration is not very meaningful.

### Printed p. 695

*Running head: [Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 6, Varga 10] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā; p. 695.*

असिन्वन् दंष्ट्रैः पितुः अत्ति भोजनं (*asinvan daṃṣṭraiḥ pituḥ atti bhojanaṃ*) — The meaning that the commentator has given for this sentence is not suited to the context and is contrary to Yāska's explanation. The commentator's Sanskrit says, in substance: the world, doing works such as dam-building, eats with its teeth the water that has come from the protecting heaven, and the plants that come from it; or the fire, not being engaged, eats with its tooth-like flames the food in the form of oblation belonging to the sacrificer who protects it. That is to say, the world, or the people of the world, doing works such as the building of bridges, eat with their teeth the food in the form of water, falling as rain from the protecting atmosphere (heaven), or the food that arises from that water, the plants (grain produced from trees and plants); or the fire, friendly to the sacrificer, eats, that is, burns, with its flames, which are like teeth, the oblation-food that the sacrificer offers in it. Two kinds of meaning have been given.

A little examination of these sentence-meanings is necessary. Here the commentator's explanation of the word असिन्वन् (*asinvan*) as "doing works such as dam-building", that is, building bridges and the like, does not help the sense indicated in this sentence. Though the people of the world eat rain-water or the food produced from it, there is no connection at all between building bridges and eating food. Therefore Yāska, rejecting the meaning "works such as dam-building" for the word असिन्वन् (*asinvan*), quotes a Ṛk in which the same word is used (Ṛk 10-79-1, as supplied "Pu. Saṃ. 10-79-1"), and gives for the word असिन्वती (*asinvatī*) in it the etymology असिन्वती असंखादंत्यौ (*asinvatī asaṃkhādaṃtyau*) (Nirukta 6-4). Durgācārya explains in his commentary that असंखादंत्यौ (*asaṃkhādaṃtyau*) means "eating as if not crushing well", that is, eating without chewing well. If the same meaning is given to the word असिन्वन् (*asinvan*) in the present Ṛk, the sentence असिन्वन् दंष्ट्रैः पितुः अत्ति (*asinvan daṃṣṭraiḥ pituḥ atti*) comes to mean that the people of the world eat hurriedly, without chewing well with the teeth (because they are hungry), the rain-water obtained from the protecting atmosphere, or the food produced from it [the supplied text reads नृष्युदक (*nṛṣyudaka*) here, probably for वृष्ट्युदक (*vṛṣṭyudaka*); reported, not changed]. This meaning appears to be the proper one. Sāyaṇa himself, in his commentary on the Ṛk quoted above as an illustration, has given for the word असिन्वती (*asinvatī*) the same meaning, असंखादंत्यौ (*asaṃkhādaṃtyau*), following Yāska's etymology. Why only here he has given the word असिन्वन् (*asinvan*) an unnecessary or unclear meaning is not known. In the meaning referring to Agni also, Yāska's

### Printed p. 696

*Running head: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā; Maṇḍala 2, Adhyāya 2, Sūkta 13; p. 696.*

explanation alone fits properly. For in the illustrating Ṛk this word is used with reference to Agni. And in the Ṛk (as supplied, "Ma. Saṃ. 10-79-2") that begins गुहा शिरो निहितमृधगक्षी (*guhā śiro nihitamṛdhagakṣī*) also, the commentator has explained the word असिन्वन् (*asinvan*) as असिन्वन् दंतैरसंखादजिह्वया (*asinvan daṃtairasaṃkhādajihvayā*). Here too the meaning refers to Agni: when Agni burns the oblation or the forests, it does not chew slowly with its teeth (flames) but spreads quickly and eats, that is, burns; the word असिन्वन् (*asinvan*) seems to be used in this sense. Therefore the meaning referring to Agni that the commentator has given in the present Ṛk may be the Ṛṣi's intention. Moreover, though the word असिन्वन् (*asinvan*) is used in the Ṛks Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-39-6 and 8-45-38, there the commentator has explained the sense taking the word to be formed from a root meaning "to throw" (असु-क्षेपणे (*asu-kṣepaṇe*)).
