**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> हे इंद्र अध आपि च त्वं दिवे द्योतमानाय सूर्याय पृथिवीं चलितां
> सतीं दृढीकृत्य संदृशे संदर्शनीयामकृणोः । अकरोः ॥ दृशे विख्ये चेति
> केन्प्रत्ययांतत्वेन निपातितः ॥ यश्च त्वं धौतीनां चलंतीनां नदीनां पथो
> मार्गानरिणक् । अरेचयः । गंतुं योग्यानकरोरित्यर्थः ॥ रुचिर् विरेचने । लजु
> सिप् । तस्य हल्बादिना लोपः ॥ अहिहन् अहेर्वत्रस्य मेघस्य वा हंतर्हे इंद्र
> देवाः स्तोतारस्तं तादृशं देवं त्वां स्तोमेभिः स्तोत्रैरजनन् । तत्र दृष्टांतः ।
> उदभिर्न वाजिनं । यथा वाजिनमश्वमुदभिरुदकैर्वर्धयंति तद्वत् ॥ पद्दन्नोमा-
> सित्यादिनोदकस्योदन्भावः ॥ शेषं सिद्धं ॥

*Gist: O Indra, you made the earth firm and visible to the shining sun and opened paths for the flowing rivers; the gods praised you thus, as men strengthen a horse with water.*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

इंद्र (*iṃdra*) — O Indra. अध (*adha*) — besides the extraordinary deeds told above. दिवे (*dive*) — for the shining sun. पृथिवीं (*pṛthivīṃ*) — the earth. संदृशे (*saṃdṛśe*) — so as to be fit for sight. अकृणोः (*akṛṇoḥ*) — you made. यः (*yaḥ*) — you who. धौतीनां (*dhautīnāṃ*) — of the flowing rivers. पथः (*pathaḥ*) — the paths. अरिणक् (*ariṇak*) — have laid out. अहिहन् (*ahihan*) — O Indra, slayer of Vṛtra. देवं तं त्वा (*devaṃ taṃ tvā*) — you, such a one, of divine nature. देवाः (*devāḥ*) — the praisers. वाजिनं (*vājinaṃ*) — a horse. उदभिर्न (*udabhirna*) — as one makes it strong with water. स्तोमेभिः (*stomebhiḥ*) — with praises. अजनन् (*ajanan*) — made you grow. सः (*saḥ*) — such you. उक्ष्यः आसि (*ukṣyaḥ āsi*) — are worthy of praise.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O Indra, besides the extraordinary deeds described above, you made the earth fit to be seen by the shining sun. You who laid out the paths of the flowing rivers, O Indra, slayer of Vṛtra, such a one of divine nature, the praisers made to grow with praises, as one makes a horse strong with water. Such a one you are worthy of praise.

**Printed English**

Inasmuch as you have rendered earth visible to heaven, and set open the path of the rivers by slaying Ahi; therefore the gods have rendered you divine by praises, as(men) invigorate a horse by water; (and) you are;(Indra), to be praised.

### Printed p. 698

*Running head: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā; Maṇḍala 2, Adhyāya 2, Sūkta 13; p. 698.*

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

अध अकृणोः पृथिवीं संदृशे दिवे (*adha akṛṇoḥ pṛthivīṃ saṃdṛśe dive*) — The commentator's Sanskrit (हे इंद्र अध अपि च त्वं दिवे द्योतमानाय सूर्याय पृथिवीं चलितां सतीं दृढीकृत्य संदृशे संदर्शनीयामकृणोः (*he iṃdra adha api ca tvaṃ dive dyotamānāya sūryāya pṛthivīṃ calitāṃ satīṃ dṛḍhīkṛtya saṃdṛśe saṃdarśanīyāmakṛṇoḥ*)) is explained in the Kannada: "O Indra, you made this trembling earth firm and unmoving, and made it visible to the sun shining in the atmosphere." That is the commentator's meaning. Another kind of meaning can also be given: you struck with the thunderbolt Vṛtra, or the clouds, spread in the atmosphere between the earth and the sun, made the water fall on the earth as rain, destroyed the clouds that had covered the atmosphere so that the sun was not seen, and made the earth visible to the sun. When cloud has gathered in the atmosphere and it is dark, the sun is not seen, and the earth is not seen by the sun. On such an occasion, by destroying the clouds through producing rain, the atmosphere becomes clear without any covering, and so the earth is well visible to the sun; this is the main intention.

यः धौतीनां अहिहन् अरिणक् पथः (*yaḥ dhautīnāṃ ahihan ariṇak pathaḥ*) — Here the commentator's Sanskrit (यश्च त्वं धौतीनां चलंतीनां नदीनां पथो मार्गानरिणक् । अरेचयः । गंतुं योग्यानकरोरित्यर्थः (*yaśca tvaṃ dhautīnāṃ calaṃtīnāṃ nadīnāṃ patho mārgānariṇak | arecayaḥ | gaṃtuṃ yogyānakarorityarthaḥ*)) is followed by the Kannada: O Indra, you slew Vṛtra the Asura, or the clouds, who had held back the rain in the atmosphere, made the rain fall on the earth, and laid out the way by which those rain waters go and join the sea. All the rain water falling on the earth joins a river. The river flows in its own, that is, a definite channel, and goes and joins the sea. Since the river water ordinarily flows to the sea along a definite path (or one that gradually slopes down), and since that path remains always the same without change, the main intention is that Indra built that definite path along which the river flows. [The supplied text has "ಮೇಘಗಗಳನ್ನು" for the clouds; reported, not changed.]

अहिहन् (*ahihan*) — अहेर्वत्रस्य मेघस्य वा हंतः (*ahervatrasya meghasya vā haṃtaḥ*): Vṛtra the Asura or the cloud. Because Indra is the destroyer of these, he is addressed by the word अहिहन् (*ahihan*).

तं त्वा स्तोमेभिः उदभिः न वाजिनं देवं देवा अजनन् (*taṃ tvā stomebhiḥ udabhiḥ na vājinaṃ devaṃ devā ajanan*) — O Indra, the commentator's explanation is that the gods sing your qualities with praises and the like and make you endowed with qualities, as one makes a horse grow with waters. The meaning of this sentence is not clear. The main intention is that the gods praise you (Indra) with hymns and that Indra's power grows by hymns. It is the custom of the seers to say that when praise is offered, the power of the gods

### Printed p. 699

*Running head: [Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 6, Varga 11] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā; p. 699.*

greatly increases or shines. Many sentences are found here and there with the sense त्वां वर्धंतु नो गिरः (*tvāṃ vardhaṃtu no giraḥ*), "may our words of praise, or hymns, cause you (Indra) to grow (praise you)". The illustration उदभिः न वाजिनं (*udabhiḥ na vājinaṃ*) given to make the sense of this sentence clear does not accord with the meaning; what the right meaning of "as a horse is made to grow with waters" is, cannot be known. Probably it may be explained as: as giving water to a horse tired by walking a long distance removes its fatigue and brings back its former strength, or as washing with water a horse that looked dirty with dust and the like makes it look well. But these meanings do not fit this context properly.

#### Ṛk 6

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> यो भोज॑नं च॒ दय॑से च॒ वर्ध॑नमा॒र्दारदा शुष्कं॒ मधु॑मद्दु॒दोहि॑थ ।
> सः शे॑व॒धिं नि द॑धिषे वि॒वस्व॑ति॒ विश्व॒स्यैक॑ ईशिषे॒ सास्यु॒क्थ्यः॑ ॥ ६ ॥

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> यः । भोजनं । च । दयसे । च । वर्धनं । आर्द्रात् । आ । शुष्कं । मधुमत् । दुदोहिथ ।
> सः । शेव्यधिं । नि । दधिषे । विवस्वति । विश्वस्य । एकः । ईशिषे । सः । असि । उक्तः ॥ ६ ॥

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> हे इंद्र यस्त्वं भोजनं । भुज्यत इति भोजनमन्नादि । च दयसे । यज-
> मानेभ्यः प्रयच्छसि ॥ दय दानगतिरक्षणहिंसाग्रहणेषु आत्मनेपदी ॥ किंच वर्धनं
> वृद्धिकरं धनं बलं वा दयसे । तथाद्र्रात्कांडात् शुष्कमनाद्रं प्रीह्यादिकं
> मधुमत् मधुररसोपेतं दुदोहिथ । दुग्धवानसि ॥ दुहेर्लिटि क्रादिनियमादि-
> डागमः ॥ स तादृशस्त्वं विवस्वति ते परिचरणं कुर्वाणे यजमाने शेवधिं धनसदनं
> निदधिषे । निदधासि । किं बहुना । विश्वस्य सर्वस्य जगत एकोद्वितीय एव सन् ईशिषे ।
> स्वामी भवसि ॥ ईश ऐश्वर्ये । ईशः स इतीडागमः ॥ स इत्यादि सिद्धं ॥

*Gist: Indra gives food and strengthening wealth to the sacrificers, milks sweet juice even from dry stalks, places wealth in the house of the one who serves him, and rules alone over the whole world.*

### Printed p. 700

*Running head: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā; Maṇḍala 2, Adhyāya 2, Sūkta 13; p. 700.*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

(इंद्र (*iṃdra*) — O Indra.) यः (*yaḥ*) — you who. भोजनं (*bhojanaṃ*) — food and the like. दयसे (*dayase*) — you give (to the sacrificers and others). च (*ca*) — and. वर्धनं च (*vardhanaṃ ca*) — wealth and strength that cause increase, too, you give; (likewise). आद्र्रात् (*ādrrāt*) — from the moist stalk. शुष्कं (*śuṣkaṃ*) — dried grain and the like. मधुमत् (*madhumat*) — as endowed with sweet juice. दुदोहिथ (*dudohitha*) — you have milked. सः (*saḥ*) — such you. विवस्वति (*vivasvati*) — in the sacrificer who offers you service. शेवधिं (*śevadhiṃ*) — a treasure of wealth. नि दधिषे (*ni dadhiṣe*) — you lay down. (And) विश्वस्य (*viśvasya*) — of the whole world. एकः (*ekaḥ*) — being without a second. ईशिषे (*īśiṣe*) — you are the lord. सः (*saḥ*) — such you. उक्त्यः असि (*uktyaḥ asi*) — are worthy of praise.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O Indra, you who give the sacrificers and others food and the like, and also wealth and strength that cause increase; and who, as it were, milk from the moist stalk dried grain endowed with sweet juice, such a one as you lay down a treasure of wealth in the sacrificer who offers you service. You are the one, unequalled lord of the whole world; such an excellent one, you are worthy of praise.

**Printed English**

(You are he) who bestow both food and increase, and milk the dry nutritious(grain) from out the humid stalk: he, who gives wealth to the worshipper, and are sole sovereign of the Universe; you are he,(Indra), who is to be praised.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

यो भोजनं च दयसे च वर्धनं (*yo bhojanaṃ ca dayase ca vardhanaṃ*) — भुज्यत इति भोजनमन्नादि (*bhujyata iti bhojanamannādi*) and the rest (the commentator's Sanskrit, as in the Bhāṣya above). The meaning is: Indra, you give the sacrificers who perform sacrifice, or the priests who sing praises, food and the like, and wealth or strength that grows.

आद्र्रात् आ शुष्कं मधुमत् मुदोहिथ (*ādrrāt ā śuṣkaṃ madhumat mudohitha*) — तथाद्र्रात्कांडात् शुष्कमनार्द्रं व्रीह्यादिकं मधुमत् मधुररसोपेतं दुदोहिथ दुग्धवानसि (*tathādrrātkāṃḍāt śuṣkamanārdraṃ vrīhyādikaṃ madhumat madhurarasopetaṃ dudohitha dugdhavānasi*) (the commentator's Sanskrit). Sāyaṇa's explanation is that you provide, from the moist stalk, grain such as rice that is well dried and agreeable. In this sentence there is no word that denotes grain; yet the commentator supplies that word and explains the meaning. Or, if it be thought that the seer's intention may be that you produce sweet Soma juice from the moist Soma creeper, then the word शुष्कं (*śuṣkaṃ*) would have no meaning. In short, the meaning of this sentence is not clear.

### Printed p. 701

*Running head: [Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 6, Varga 11] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā; p. 701.*

शेवधिं (*śevadhiṃ*) — The word शेवं (*śevaṃ*) is read among the names for happiness (Ni. 3-13). The commentator explains शेवधिं (*śevadhiṃ*) as धनसदनं (*dhanasadanaṃ*) a treasure, that is, an immense heap of wealth. Since happiness is obtained from wealth, this meaning too may be given.

विश्वस्य एक ईशिषे (*viśvasya eka īśiṣe*) — सर्वस्य जगत एकोऽद्वितीय एव सन् ईशिषे स्वामी भवसि (*sarvasya jagata eko 'dvitīya eva san īśiṣe svāmī bhavasi*) (the commentator's Sanskrit). You alone are the lord of the entire universe. There is no other equal to you. You are the master of all: thus Indra's greatness is described.

#### Ṛk 7

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> यः पु॒ष्पिणी॑श्च प्र॒स्व॑श्च॒ धर्म॒णाधि॒ दाने॒ व्य१॒॑गवनी॒रधा॑रयः ।
> यश्चास॑मा॒ अज॑नो दि॒द्युतो॑ दि॒व उ॒रुरू॒र्वा अ॒भितः॒ सास्यु॒क्थ्यः॑ ॥ ७ ॥

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> यः । पुष्पिणीः । च । प्रस्वः । च । धर्मणा । अधि । दाने । वि । अवनीः । अधारयः ।
> यः । च । असमाः । अजनः । दिद्युतः । दिवः । उरुः । ऊर्वान् । अभितः । सः । असि ।
> उक्थ्यः ॥ ७ ॥

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> हे इंद्र यस्त्वं पुष्पिणीः पुष्पवतीश्च प्रस्वः प्रसूताः प्रसूयमाना नाव-
> नीरवित्रीरोषधीर्दानेऽधि ॥ उपलूयंते सस्यान्यत्रेति दानं क्षेत्रं । अधिकरणे
> ल्युट् ॥ तस्मिन् क्षेत्रे धर्मणा सकललक्षणेन कर्मणा व्यधारयः । न्यदधाः । यश्च
> त्वं दिवो द्योतमानस्य सूयस्यासमा विषमा नानाप्रकारा दिद्युतो दीप्तीरजनः ।
> अजनयः । यद्वा दिवो नक्षत्राणि ॥ जनेर्लजः व्यत्ययेन शप् ॥ यश्चोरुर्महां-
> स्त्वमभितः सर्वत ऊर्वान् महतः प्राणिनिकायान् पर्वतान्वाजनयः शिष्टं स्पष्टं ॥

*Gist: Indra established flowering and fruiting plants in the field by proper rite, created the sun's varied rays, and made vast creatures; he is to be praised.*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

(इंद्र (*iṃdra*) — O Indra.) यः (*yaḥ*) — you who. पुष्पिणीः (*puṣpiṇīḥ*) — those endowed with flowers. च (*ca*) — and. प्रस्वः (*prasvaḥ*) — those that yield fruits. अवनीः (*avanīḥ*) — the plants. दाने अधि (*dāne adhi*) — in the field.

### Printed p. 702

*Running head: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā; Maṇḍala 2, Adhyāya 2, Sūkta 13 (as printed "ಸೂ. ೩"); p. 702.*

धर्मणा (*dharmaṇā*) — by a rite endowed with all characteristics. वि आधारयः (*vi ādhārayaḥ*) — you have established. च (*ca*) — moreover. यः (*yaḥ*) — you who. दिवः (*divaḥ*) — of the shining sun. असमाः (*asamāḥ*) — of many kinds. दिद्युतः (*didyutaḥ*) — the rays. अजनः (*ajanaḥ*) — you created (and). उरुः (*uruḥ*) — being of vast body. अभितः (*abhitaḥ*) — all around. ऊर्वान् (*ūrvān*) — great multitudes of creatures too you created. सः (*saḥ*) — such. (you,) उक्त्यः असि (*uktyaḥ asi*) — are worthy of praise.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O Indra, you who by a rite endowed with all characteristics have established in the field the plants that are endowed with flowers and yield fruits; moreover, who have created the many kinds of rays of the shining sun (and likewise the stars), and, being of vast body, have created great multitudes of creatures: such a one you are worthy of praise.

**Printed English**

You have caused, by culture, the flowering and fruitful(plants) to spread over the field; you have generated the varions [sic] luminaries of heaven; and who, of vast bulk, comprehend vast‘(bodies); yon [sic] are he who is to be praised.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

यः पुष्टिणीः च प्रस्वः च धर्मणा अधि दाने वि अवनीः आधारयः (*yaḥ puṣṭiṇīḥ ca prasvaḥ ca dharmaṇā adhi dāne vi avanīḥ ādhārayaḥ*) — पुष्पवतीक्ष्य प्रसूयमाना अवनीरवित्रीरोषधीर्दाने क्षेत्रे सकललक्षणेन कर्मणा न्यदधाः (*puṣpavatīkṣya prasūyamānā avanīravitrīroṣadhīrdāne kṣetre sakalalakṣaṇena karmaṇā nyadadhāḥ*) (the commentator's Sanskrit; the supplied text has पुष्टिणीः (*puṣṭiṇīḥ*) for पुष्पिणीः (*puṣpiṇīḥ*) and पुष्पवतीक्ष्य (*puṣpavatīkṣya*), reported, not changed). In this sentence the commentator has taken the word दान (*dāna*) to mean a field (land, a plot), अवनीः (*avanīḥ*) to mean plants (rice and similar crops), and धर्मणा (*dharmaṇā*) to mean by a rite endowed with all characteristics. If these meanings are accepted, the sentence means: O Indra, you have set up natural cosmic laws by which the plants and the like that grow in fields, paddies and so on, in whatever seasons and in whatever manner they should grow and increase, first put forth flowers and afterwards bear fruit. That is, plants, trees, creepers and the like, subject to your regulation, continue without fail to perform such functions as flowering and fruiting at their proper seasons: this is the main intention.

यः च असमाः अजनः दिद्युतः दिवः उरुः ऊर्वान् अभितः (*yaḥ ca asamāḥ ajanaḥ didyutaḥ divaḥ uruḥ ūrvān abhitaḥ*) — In this sentence also the meaning must be given by supposing some words. The various kinds of rays of the sun

### Printed p. 703

*Running head: [Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 6, Varga 11] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā; p. 703.*

(The Special Topics of Ṛk 7 continues:) ...the kinds of light that appear in the morning, at midday and in the evening, and the great trees, animals, mountains, rivers and so on seen everywhere: Indra is addressed and described as having created all these.

#### Ṛk 8

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> यो ना॑र्म॒रं स॒हव॑सुं॒ निहं॑तवे पृ॒क्षाय॑ च दा॒सवे॑शाय॒ चाव॑हः ।
> ऊ॒र्जयं॑त्या॒ अप॑रिविष्टमा॒स्य॑मु॒तैवाद्य पु॑रुकृ॒त्सास्यु॒क्थ्यः॑ ॥ ८ ॥

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> यः । नार्मरं । सहऽवसुं । निऽहंतवे । पृक्षाय । च । दासऽवेशाय । च । अवहः ।
> ऊर्जयंत्याः । अपरिऽविष्टं । आस्यं । उत । एव । अद्य । पुरुऽकृत् । सः । असि ।
> उक्थ्यः ॥ ८ ॥

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> पुरुकृत् पुरूणां कर्मणां कर्ता हे इंद्र यस्त्वं नार्मरं । न्यून् मनु-
> ष्यान्मारयतीति नृमरः कश्चिदसुरः । तस्यापत्यं नार्मरः । तं सहवसुं । वसुना सह
> वर्तत इति सहवसुः । असुरनामैतत् । एतन्नामकमसुरं निहंतवे ॥ हंतेस्तुमर्थे
> तवेन्प्रत्ययः । तादौ च नितीति गतेः प्रकृतिस्वरत्वं ॥ निहंतुं ऊर्जयंत्या बलवत्या
> वज्रधाराया अपरिविष्टं मलादिभिरव्याप्तमास्यमद्यॆनावहः । तमसुरं प्रापयः ।
> यद्वा ऊर्जयंत्याः पिशाचिकाया आस्यं प्रापयः । किमर्थं । पृक्षाय । तव हवि-
> र्लक्षणान्नलाभाय । दासवेशाय दासानां दस्यूनां वेशाय विनाशाय च । यद्वा
> अस्माकमन्नलाभाय दस्युविनाशाय च ॥

*Gist: Indra, doer of many deeds, bore a pure face to slay the asura Sahavasu, son of Nṛmara, for food and the destruction of the Dasyus; he is worthy of praise.*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

पुरुकृत् (*purukṛt*) — O Indra, who have done unusual and manifold deeds. यः (*yaḥ*) — you who. पृक्षाय (*pṛkṣāya*) — for the gain of food in the form of the oblation. दासवेशाय च (*dāsaveśāya ca*) — and also for the destruction of the Dasyus. नार्मरं (*nārmaraṃ*) — the son of Nṛmara, सहवसुं (*sahavasuṃ*) — bearing the name Sahavasu, the son of an asura (continued on the next page).

### Printed p. 704

*Running head: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā; Maṇḍala 2, Adhyāya 2, Sūkta 13 (as printed "ಸೂ ೧೩"); p. 704.*

निहंतवे (*nihaṃtave*) — in order to kill. ऊर्जयंत्याः (*ūrjayaṃtyāḥ*) — strong, having the form of the edge of the thunderbolt, अपरिविष्टं (*apariviṣṭaṃ*) — and free from dirt: अस्यं (*asyaṃ*) [as supplied] — the face. अद्य एव (*adya eva*) — at once. अवहः (*avahaḥ*) — you bore. सः (*saḥ*) — such a you. उक्त्यः (*uktyaḥ*) [as supplied] — worthy of praise. असि (*asi*) — are.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O Indra, doer of many extraordinary deeds, you who, for the gain of food and the destruction of the Dasyus, at once took on a face in the form of the edge of the thunderbolt, free of dirt, to kill Sahavasu, the son of Nṛmara, such a one you are worthy of praise.

**Printed English**

You, who are(famed for) many exploits, put on to-day an unclouded countenance,(as prepared) to slay Sahavasu, the son of Nrimara, with the sharpened(edge of the thunderbolt), in defence of the(sacrificial) food, and for the destruction of the Dasyns [sic]; you are he who is to be praised.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

नार्मरं—न्यन् मनुष्यान् मारयतीति नृमरः कश्चिदसुरः (*nārmaraṃ—nyan manuṣyān mārayatīti nṛmaraḥ kaścidasuraḥ*) — the name of an asura. Because he kills men he is commonly called by the name Nṛmara. His son is called Nārmara. This word occurs in the Ṛgveda only in the present Ṛk and nowhere else, so nothing more can be said about him. The scholar Ludwig takes the word ऊर्जयंती (*ūrjayaṃtī*) in this Ṛk to mean a strong fort, and holds that Nārmara was the king, lord of that fort or stronghold; but this view has no adequate support.

सहवसुं (*sahavasuṃ*) — the son of the asura named Nṛmara. Little is known of him either. The commentator, giving the word's component meaning वसुना सह वर्तत इति सहवसुः (*vasunā saha vartata iti sahavasuḥ*), explains it as "the asura Sahavasu, who possesses much wealth".

दासवेशाय (*dāsaveśāya*) — दासानां दस्यूनां वेशाय विनाशाय (*dāsānāṃ dasyūnāṃ veśāya vināśāya*): for destroying the wicked Dasyu people.

पृक्षाय (*pṛkṣāya*) — the word पृक्ष (*pṛkṣa*) is read among the names of food (Ni. 3-9). The commentator gives two senses: for gaining the food in the form of the oblation which we offer to you, or for the food which you give us.

### Printed p. 705

*Running head: [Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 6, Varga 11] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā; p. 705.*

ऊर्जयंत्याः अपरिविष्टं आस्यं उत एव अद्य (*ūrjayaṃtyāḥ apariviṣṭaṃ āsyaṃ uta eva adya*) — for the word अपरिविष्टं (*apariviṣṭaṃ*) in this sentence the explanation given is मलादिभिरव्याप्तं (*malādibhiravyāptaṃ*): without dirt, pure. What the right sense of the sentence is, and the seer's intention, is not clear. Perhaps the intention is that Indra, to destroy the asura Sahavasu, son of Nṛmara, took on a form (shape) full of radiance and power and so destroyed that asura.

#### Ṛk 9

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> श॒तं वा॒ यस्य॒ दश॑ सा॒कमाद्य॒ एक॑स्य श्रु॒ष्टौ यद्ध॑ चो॒दमावि॑थ ।
> अ॒र॒ज्ञौ दस्यू॒न्त्समु॑नब्द॒भीत॑ये सुप्रा॒व्यो॑ अभवः॒ सास्यु॒क्थ्यः॑ ॥ ९ ॥

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> शतं । वा । यस्य । दश । साकं । आ । अद्यः । एकस्य । श्रुष्टौ । यत् । ह । चोदं । आविथ ।
> अरज्ञौ । दस्यून् । सं । उनप् । दभीतये । सुप्रऽआव्यः । अभवः । सः । असि ।
> उक्थ्यः ॥ ९ ॥

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> हे इंद्र एकस्यॆकाकिनः श्रेष्ठस्य वा यस्य ते श्रुष्टौ सुखनिमित्ते तदर्थं शतं
> दश दश शतानि हरयो वाहनार्थं भवंति । तथा च मंत्रवर्णः । इंद्रो मायाभिः
> पुरुरूप ईयते युक्ता ह्यस्य हरयः शता दश । ६-४७-१८ । इति । अपि च यश्च आ
> अद्यः सर्वेषां सर्वत उपजीव्यः। न तस्येशे यं नाद्याद्यद्वैनं नाद्युरिति हि श्रुतिः ।
> यद्ध यश्च त्वं चोदं स्तोत्राणां प्रेरकं यजमानमाविथ । रक्षितवानसि । किंच
> यस्त्वमरज् रज्जुवर्जिते बंधनागारे दस्यनुपक्षपयित्थन् दभीतये । दभीति-
> र्नाम कश्चि दृषिः । तदर्थं समुनप् । हिंसितवानसि ॥ उभतेर्हिंसाकर्मणो लजु
> व्यत्ययेन श्नम् । हल्च्या दिना सिपो लोपः । अडभावश्कांदसः ॥ किंच सुप्राव्यः
> सुखेन सर्वैरुपसर्पणीयोऽभवः । शिष्टं सिद्धं ॥

> *he iṃdra ekasyèkākinaḥ śreṣṭhasya vā yasya te śruṣṭau sukhanimitte tadarthaṃ śataṃ*
> *daśa daśa śatāni harayo vāhanārthaṃ bhavaṃti | tathā ca maṃtravarṇaḥ | iṃdro māyābhiḥ*
> *pururūpa īyate yuktā hyasya harayaḥ śatā daśa | 6-47-18 | iti | api ca yaśca ā*
> *adyaḥ sarveṣāṃ sarvata upajīvyaḥ| na tasyeśe yaṃ nādyādyadvainaṃ nādyuriti hi śrutiḥ |*
> *yaddha yaśca tvaṃ codaṃ stotrāṇāṃ prerakaṃ yajamānamāvitha | rakṣitavānasi | kiṃca*
> *yastvamaraj rajjuvarjite baṃdhanāgāre dasyanupakṣapayitthan dabhītaye | dabhīti-*
> *rnāma kaści dṛṣiḥ | tadarthaṃ samunap | hiṃsitavānasi ‖ ubhaterhiṃsākarmaṇo laju*
> *vyatyayena śnam | halcyā dinā sipo lopaḥ | aḍabhāvaśkāṃdasaḥ ‖ kiṃca suprāvyaḥ*
> *sukhena sarvairupasarpaṇīyo 'bhavaḥ | śiṣṭaṃ siddhaṃ ‖*

### Printed p. 706

*Running head: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā; Maṇḍala 2, Adhyāya 2, Sūkta 13; p. 706.*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

(इंद्रॆ (*iṃdrè*) — O Indra) एकस्य (*ekasya*) — of the excellent one. यस्य (*yasya*) — of you whose. श्रुष्टौ (*śruṣṭau*) — for the pleasure. शतं दश (*śataṃ daśa*) — ten hundred (a thousand) horses are ready (you who). साकं (*sākaṃ*) — together. आ आद्यः (*ā ādyaḥ*) — you who provide food for all. यद्ध (*yaddha*) — you who. चोदं (*codaṃ*) — the sacrificer who impels the praisers. अविथ (*avitha*) — have protected. (यः (*yaḥ*) — you who) दभीतये (*dabhītaye*) — to help the sage Dabhīti. दस्यून् (*dasyūn*) — the violent asuras. अरज् (*araj*) — in a prison without ropes. समुनप् (*samunap*) — have placed and tormented. (and) सुप्राव्यः (*suprāvyaḥ*) — easily approached by all. अभवः (*abhavaḥ*) — have become. सः (*saḥ*) — such you. उत्कृष्टः असि (*utkṛṣṭaḥ asi*) — are praiseworthy.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O Indra, for the pleasure of you, the excellent one, a thousand horses are ready; you provide food for all and protect the sacrificer who impels the praisers; and you, to help the sage Dabhīti, placed the violent asuras in a prison without ropes and tormented them. Therefore you are easily approached by all, and such a you are exceedingly praiseworthy.

**Printed English translation**

You, for whose sole pleasure a thousand(steeds are ready); by whom all are to be fed; and who protect the institutor(of the sacrifice); who, for the sake of Dabhiti, have cast the Dasyus into unfettered(captivity), and who are to be approached(by all); you are he who is to be praised.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

शतं वा यस्य दश साकं आ अद्यः एकस्य श्रुष्टौ (*śataṃ vā yasya daśa sākaṃ ā adyaḥ ekasya śruṣṭau*) — here the word एकस्य (*ekasya*) means एकाकिनः श्रेष्ठस्य वा (*ekākinaḥ śreṣṭhasya vā*): for you who are one, for you alone, or for you who are excellent. O Indra, a thousand (ten hundred) horses are ready for you, the excellent or the only one, as mounts. The same idea is expressed in the Ṛk

इंद्रो मायाभिः पुरुरूप ईयते युक्ता ह्यस्य हरयः शता दश (*iṃdro māyābhiḥ pururūpa īyate yuktā hyasya harayaḥ śatā daśa*)

(M. Saṃ. 6-47-18, as printed). It says that when Indra fights the asuras he takes on many magical forms and uses thousands of horses as mounts. Here

### Printed p. 707

*Running head: [Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 6, Varga 11] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā; p. 707.*

"thousand" can mean one thousand or "many". The sage describes Indra's distinction: so many horses are ready for Indra alone.

श्रुष्टौ (*śruṣṭau*) — for the word श्रुष्टी (*śruṣṭī*): श्रुष्टीति क्षिप्रनाम आशु अष्टीति (*śruṣṭīti kṣipranāma āśu aṣṭīti*). Yāska explains श्रुष्टी (*śruṣṭī*) as "quickly", or "pervading quickly" (Ni. 6-13). Here, however, the bhāṣyakāra gives for श्रुष्टौ (*śruṣṭau*) the sense सुखनिमित्ते (*sukhanimitte*), "for pleasure".

यश्च आ आद्यः (*yaśca ā ādyaḥ*) — सर्वेषां सर्वत उपजीव्यः (*sarveṣāṃ sarvata upajīvyaḥ*). All live depending on Indra; that is, Indra provides food and the rest to all, everywhere. This is the sense.

यत् ह चोदं आविध (*yat ha codaṃ āvidha*) — यश्च त्वं चोदं स्तोत्राणां प्रेरकं यजमानं रक्षितवानसि (*yaśca tvaṃ codaṃ stotrāṇāṃ prerakaṃ yajamānaṃ rakṣitavānasi*). "Impeller of the praises" means the sacrificer who urges the priests to praise Indra; the sense is that Indra protects him.

अरज् दस्यून् सं उनप् दभीतये (*araj dasyūn saṃ unap dabhītaye*) — O Indra, to protect the sage called Dabhīti you bound and tormented the Dasyus in a prison without ropes (रज्जु (*rajju*)), says the sage. When the Dasyus were harassing the sage Dabhīti, Indra, at his prayer, fought them, put them in prison without binding them with ropes, and subjected them to many kinds of torment. In some places it is said that the Aśvins protected the sage Dabhīti, in others that Indra protected him.

याभिः कुत्समार्जुनेयं शतक्रतू प्र तुर्वितिं प्र च दभीतिमावतं (*yābhiḥ kutsamārjuneyaṃ śatakratū pra turvitiṃ pra ca dabhītimāvataṃ*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-112-23). In this Ṛk it is said that the Aśvins protected Dabhīti. In some places this Dabhīti is called a warrior, in others a sage:

इंद्रो धुनिं च चुमुरिं च दंभयञ्छ्रद्दामनस्या शृणुते दभीतये (*iṃdro dhuniṃ ca cumuriṃ ca daṃbhayañchraddāmanasyā śṛṇute dabhītaye*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-113-9)

स्वप्नेनाभ्युप्या चुमुरिं धुनिं च जघंथ दस्युं प्र दभीतिमावः (*svapnenābhyupyā cumuriṃ dhuniṃ ca jaghaṃtha dasyuṃ pra dabhītimāvaḥ*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-15-9)

In these Ṛks Dabhīti is called a royal sage, and it is said that for him Indra conquered the asuras Chumuri and Dhuni. It is understood that he pressed and offered Soma juice to Indra and obtained Indra's favour.

### Printed p. 708

*Running head: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā; Maṇḍala 2, Adhyāya 2, Sūkta 13; p. 708.*

अस्वापयद्धभीतये सहस्रा त्रिशतं हथैः । दासानामिंद्रो मायया (*asvāpayaddhabhītaye sahasrā triśataṃ hathaiḥ | dāsānāmiṃdro māyayā*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-30-21). In this Ṛk it is said that Indra by his magic put thirty thousand Dāsas to sleep for Dabhīti.

#### Ṛk 10

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> विश्वेदनु॑ रोध॒ना अ॑स्य॒ पौंस्यं॑ द॒दुर॑स्मै दधि॒रे कृ॒त्स्नवे॒ धनं॑ ।
> षळ॑स्तभ्ना वि॒ष्टिरः॒ पंच॑ सं॒दृशः॒ परि॑ प॒रो अ॑भवः॒ सास्यु॒क्थ्यः॑ ॥ १० ॥

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> विश्वा । इत् । अनु । रोधनाः । अस्य । पौंस्यं । ददुः । अस्मै । दधिरे । कृत्नवे । धनं ।
> षट् । अस्तभ्नाः । विस्तिरः । पंच । संदृशः । परि । परः । अभवः । सः । असि । उक्त्यः ॥

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> विश्वेत् ॥ सुपां सुलुगिति जस आकारः ॥ सर्वा एव रोधना रोधस्वत्यो
> नद्योऽस्येंद्रस्य पौंस्यं । पुंसो भावः पौंस्यं । वीर्यमिति यावत् । अनु
> तद्विर्यमनु वर्तंते । अस्मा इंद्राय ददुः । हविर्लक्षणमन्नं यजमानाः प्रय-
> च्छंति । किंच कृत्नवे कर्मणां कर्त्र इंद्राय धनं दधिरे । सर्वॆ जना धारयंति ।
> तढा च मंत्रः । इंद्राय द्याव ओषधीरुतापो रयिं रक्षंति जीरयो वनानि ।
> ३-५१-५ । इति । विष्टिरो विस्तीर्णाः षट् षट्संख्याका उर्वीः । ताश्च द्यौश्च पृथिवी
> चाहश्च रात्रिश्चापश्चौषधय इत्येवंरूपाः । ता अस्तभ्नाः । नियमितवानसि । संदृशः ।
> सम्यक् पश्यंतीति संदृशो जनाः । पंच संदृशः पंच जनान् परि सर्वतः परः
> पारयिता पालयिता वाभवः । भवसि । गतमन्यत् ॥

*Gist: All the rivers flow in accordance with Indra's manly power; people give him oblations and wealth; he has restrained the six wide worlds and protects the five peoples.*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

विश्वा इत् (*viśvā it*) — all. रोधनाः (*rodhanāḥ*) — the rivers. अस्य (*asya*) — of you who are Indra. पौंस्यं (*pauṃsyaṃ*) — the heroic deed. अनु (*anu*) — following (as its result) they flow. अस्मै (*asmai*) — to you, such an Indra. ददुः (*daduḥ*) — (the sacrificers) offer (the oblation). कृत्नवे (*kṛtnave*) — to you, the doer of excellent deeds. धनं (*dhanaṃ*) — wealth. दधिरे (*dadhire*) — (all) offer. विस्तिरः (*vistiraḥ*) — wide (the entry breaks off here at the end of the page; it continues on the next page).

### Printed p. 709

*Running head: Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 6, Varga 11; Ṛgveda-saṃhitā; p. 709.*

(Pratipadārtha of Ṛk 10, continued from the previous page.) विस्तिरः (*vistiraḥ*) — you who are pervading widely. षट् (*ṣaṭ*) — the six creations of yours, earth and the rest, six in number. अस्तभ्नाः (*astabhnāḥ*) — you have kept under control. पंच संदृशः (*paṃca saṃdṛśaḥ*) — the five peoples. परि (*pari*) — everywhere. परः (*paraḥ*) — as protector. अभवः (*abhavaḥ*) — you have become. सः (*saḥ*) — such a you. उक्ष्यः आसि (*ukṣyaḥ āsi*) — you are worthy of praise (as printed here उक्ष्यः (*ukṣyaḥ*); the Saṃhitā and Pada of Ṛk 10 read उक्थ्यः (*ukthyaḥ*) / उक्त्यः (*uktyaḥ*)).

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O Indra, all the rivers, in the form of Indra, flow following your heroic deed and as its result. The sacrificers offer oblations to you. They offer wealth to you, the supreme doer of deeds. You who pervade widely have kept under control the six creations of yours, earth and the rest, six in number; and you protect the five peoples everywhere. Such a you are exceedingly worthy of praise.

**Printed English translation of Ṛk 10**

You are he, from whose manhood all the rivers(have proceeded); to whom(the pions) have given(offerings); to whom, doer of mighty deeds, they have presented wealth: you are he, who have regulated the six expan- sive(objects), and are the protector of the five(races), that look up to you: you are he who is to be praised.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

विश्वा इत् अनु रोधनाः अस्य पौंस्यं (*viśvā it anu rodhanāḥ asya pauṃsyaṃ*) — here रोधनाः (*rodhanāḥ*) means रोधस्वत्यो नद्यः (*rodhasvatyo nadyaḥ*), the rivers that flow each in its own bed, that is, between two banks. पौंस्यं (*pauṃsyaṃ*) means पुंसो भावः (*puṃso bhāvaḥ*), the manly power that should be natural to men, or an excess of ability. All the rivers flow following Indra's manly power, that is, his exceeding ability. The sense is that the rivers flow in their beds only through Indra's ability.

ददु: अस्मै (*dadu: asmai*) — हविर्लक्षणमन्नं इंद्राय यजमानाः प्रयच्छंति (*havirlakṣaṇamannaṃ iṃdrāya yajamānāḥ prayacchaṃti*). At the sacrifice the sacrificers offer food in the form of oblation, with Indra as its object.

दधिरे कृत्स्नवे धनं (*dadhire kṛtsnave dhanaṃ*) — कृत्स्नवे कर्मणां कर्त्र इंद्राय धनं दधिरे । सर्वॆ जना धारयंति (*kṛtsnave karmaṇāṃ kartra iṃdrāya dhanaṃ dadhire | sarvè janā dhārayaṃti*). Here the word कृत्स्नवे (*kṛtsnave*) is explained as कर्मणां कर्त्र इंद्राय (*karmaṇāṃ kartra iṃdrāya*), that is, "for Indra who performs deeds of daring". For the word सुरूपकृत्नुं (*surūpakṛtnuṃ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-4-1) the commentator explained the word कृत्सु (*kṛtsu*) in the same manner as is said here: शोभनरूपोपेतस्य कर्मणः कर्तारमिंद्रं (*śobhanarūpopetasya karmaṇaḥ kartāramiṃdraṃ*). Therefore the sense of this sentence is that the people, or the sacrificer and priests, offer wealth for Indra, who performs many deeds of daring such as the slaying of Vṛtra, that is, wealth in the form of oblation or Soma at the sacrifice. In this matter,

इंद्राय द्याव ओषधीरुतापो रयिं रक्षंति जीरयो वनानि (*iṃdrāya dyāva oṣadhīrutāpo rayiṃ rakṣaṃti jīrayo vanāni*)

(Ma. [sic, as printed] Saṃ. 3-51-5)

the commentator quotes this Ṛk and explains its sense: heaven, the plants and trees, the waters, men and the trees all keep guarded the wealth that is in them (the things in the form of wealth) in order to offer it to Indra.

### Printed p. 710

*Running head: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā; Maṇḍala 2, Adhyāya 2, Sūkta 13; p. 710.*

षट् अस्तभ्नाः विस्तिरः (*ṣaṭ astabhnāḥ vistiraḥ*) — विष्टिरो विस्तीर्णाः षट् षट्संख्याका उर्वीः । ताश्च दौश्च पृथिवी चाहश्च रात्रिश्चापश्चौषधय इत्येवंरूपाः । ता अस्तभ्नाः नियमितवानसि (*viṣṭiro vistīrṇāḥ ṣaṭ ṣaṭsaṃkhyākā urvīḥ | tāśca dauśca pṛthivī cāhaśca rātriścāpaścauṣadhaya ityevaṃrūpāḥ | tā astabhnāḥ niyamitavānasi*). The six kinds of wide regions are subject to you: heaven, earth, day, night, water, and the plants and trees. All these six kinds are extremely extensive, that is, their range is very great; yet Indra is the controller of them all. This is the meaning.

पंच संदृशः परि परः अभवः (*paṃca saṃdṛśaḥ pari paraḥ abhavaḥ*) — for the word संदृशः (*saṃdṛśaḥ*) in this sentence the commentator says सम्यक् पश्यंतीति संदृशो जनाः (*samyak paśyaṃtīti saṃdṛśo janāḥ*): because they are able to see well (or to understand), संदृश (*saṃdṛśa*) is explained as "people", and पंचसंदृशः (*paṃcasaṃdṛśaḥ*) as the five peoples. By the five peoples some mean five kinds of people, Gandharvas, Pitṛs, gods, Asuras and Rākṣasas; according to Upamanyu and others they are five kinds of people consisting of Brāhmaṇa, Kṣatriya, Vaiśya, Śūdra and the Niṣādas, the hunter caste. Sāyaṇa has approved this. The authors of the Nirukta say that Niṣādas are those who kill animals, or that they are called Niṣāda because sin is full in them. Besides, there may have been in that time five main tribes or peoples (janapadas). A detailed account of these five peoples and Yāska's explanation in this matter we have written in Ṛ. Saṃ. part 2, p. 296; part 8, p. 227; part 9, p. 321; part 13, p. 407. The main sense is that you, Indra, bring such five peoples out of trouble, or protect them.

#### Ṛk 11

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> सु॒प्र॒वा॒च॒नं तव॑ वीर वी॒र्यं१॒॑ यदेके॑न॒ क्रतु॑ना विं॒दसे॒ वसु॑ ।
> जा॒तूष्ठि॑रस्य॒ प्र वयः॒ सह॑स्वतो॒ या च॒कर्थ॒ सेंद्र॒ विश्वा॑स्यु॒क्थ्यः॑ ॥

> *supravācanaṃ tava vīra vīryaṃ yadekena kratunā viṃdase vasu |*
> *jātūṣṭhirasya pra vayaḥ sahasvato yā cakartha seṃdra viśvāsyukthyaḥ ‖*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> सुप्रवाचनं । तव । वीर । वीर्यं । यत् । एकेन । क्रतुना । विंदसे । वसु ।
> जातूस्थिरस्य । प्र । वयः । सहस्वतः । या । चकर्थ । सः । इंद्र । विश्वा । असि । उक्त्यः॥

> *supravācanaṃ | tava | vīra | vīryaṃ | yat | ekena | kratunā | viṃdase | vasu |*
> *jātūsthirasya | pra | vayaḥ | sahasvataḥ | yā | cakartha | saḥ | iṃdra | viśvā | asi | uktyaḥ‖*

### Printed p. 711

*Running head: Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 6, Varga 12; Ṛgveda-saṃhitā; p. 711.*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> वीर बलवन् हे इंद्र तव वीर्यं सामर्थ्यं सुप्रवाचनं । सुष्टु प्रवच-
> नीयं । सर्वै श्लाघनीयमित्यर्थः । किं तत् । एकेन क्रतुना कर्मणा वसु विंदसे ।
> शत्रूणां धनं लभसे ॥ विद्ललाभे । तुदादिः स्वरितेत् ॥ यद्वा तदीयं धनं
> स्तोत्थान्पयसीति यत् तत्पशस्यमित्यर्थः । सहस्वतो बलवतो जातूष्ठिरस्य ।
> एतन्नामकः कश्चित् । तस्य वयोऽन्नं प्रादाः । यद्वा जातूष्ठिरस्य । जातु कदाचित्
> सर्वदा स्थिरस्य सहस्वतो बलवतो यज्ञादेः कर्मणः संबंधि वयो हनिर्लक्षण-
> मन्नं प्र विंदस इति समन्वयः । या यानीमान्यन्यानि विश्वा सर्वाणि कर्माणि चकर्थ
> कृतवानसि । स तादृशस्त्वमुक्थः । सर्वैः प्रशंसनीयो भवसि ॥

*Gist: Hero Indra, your power is to be praised by all: with a single deed you win the enemies' wealth, and you take the strong, ever-steady oblation-food; by all the deeds you have done you are praiseworthy.*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

वीर (*vīra*) — O mighty Indra. यत् (*yat*) — for which reason. एकेन क्रतुना (*ekena kratunā*) — by a unique deed. वसु (*vasu*) — the wealth (of the enemy). निंदसे (*niṃdase*) — you obtain (and). सहस्वतः (*sahasvataḥ*) — which is mighty. जातूष्ठिरस्य (*jātūṣṭhirasya*) — which is ever steady. वयः (*vayaḥ*) — the food in the form of oblation. प्र (*pra*) — you eat (therefore). तव (*tava*) — your. वीर्यं (*vīryaṃ*) — power. सुप्रवाचनं (*supravācanaṃ*) — is to be praised by all. इंद्र (*iṃdra*) — O Indra. या विश्वा (*yā viśvā*) — all these deeds which. चकर्थ (*cakartha*) — you have done. सः (*saḥ*) — such a you. उक्त्यः असि (*uktyaḥ asi*) — you are worthy of praise.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O mighty Indra, your power is to be praised by all, both because by your unique deed you win the wealth of the enemy and because you partake of the oblation, which is full of vigour and ever steady. O Indra, such a you, who have done all these deeds, are worthy of praise.

**Printed English translation of Ṛk 11**

Your heroism, hero, is to be glorified, by which, with a single effort, you have acquired wealth;(wherewith) the(sacrificial) food of(every) solemn and constant(ceremony is provided); for all(the acts) you have per- formed, you Indra, are he who is to be praised.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

सुप्रवाचनं तव वीर वीर्यं (*supravācanaṃ tava vīra vīryaṃ*) — हे बलवन्निंद्र तव वीर्यं सामर्थ्यं सुष्टु प्रवचनीयं सर्वैः श्लाघनीयमित्यर्थः (*he balavanniṃdra tava vīryaṃ sāmarthyaṃ suṣṭu pravacanīyaṃ sarvaiḥ ślāghanīyamityarthaḥ*). O valiant Indra, your

### Printed p. 712

*Running head: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā; Maṇḍala 2, Adhyāya 2, Sūkta 13; p. 712.*

(Special Topics of Ṛk 11, continued from the previous page.) power is praised by all. Here "heroism" means Indra's special capacity or his deed of daring. Which deed that is, is explained in the next sentence.

यत् एकेन क्रतुना विंदसे वसु (*yat ekena kratunā viṃdase vasu*) — by one deed you gain the wealth of enemies; or, you bring that wealth to us who praise you; and that is what is to be praised. The word क्रतु (*kratu*) is read among the names for "action" (Nirukta 3-1), so क्रतुना (*kratunā*) means "by a deed" or "by a deed of daring". Defeating enemies is that deed. By one such deed, the overthrow of enemies, you acquire wealth or bring that wealth to us, your praisers. Whatever deed so defeats the enemy and brings us wealth is praised by all; this is how it connects with the previous sentence.

जातूस्थिरस्य प्र वयः सहस्वतः (*jātūsthirasya pra vayaḥ sahasvataḥ*) — you gave food (वयः (*vayaḥ*)) to Jātūsthira, who is mighty (सहस्वतः (*sahasvataḥ*)). The word सहस् (*sahas*) is read among the names for "strength" (Nirukta 3-9), so सहस्वतः (*sahasvataḥ*) means "possessing strength". O Indra, you helped a mighty man named Jātūsthira by supplying him with food; this too is one of your deeds of daring. The name Jātūsthira occurs in the Ṛgveda only in this Ṛk, nowhere else. So who he was, what his story was, and why Indra helped him with food cannot be stated. Perhaps, when this Jātūsthira was in distress without food, Indra supplied him with it at his prayer; that is what is said here.

The commentator also gives another sense (the Sanskrit alternative beginning जातूष्ठिरस्य (*jātūṣṭhirasya*)): जातु (*jātu*) "ever, always", so the word could mean a sacrifice that is steady because it is always performed by people; सहस्वतः (*sahasvataḥ*) could mean "strong", that is, endowed with greatness or giving abundant fruit. Then the meaning is: O Indra, in the sacrifices and other rites that people always perform, which give abundant fruit, you receive food in the form of oblation. But since the sense "possessing strength, valiant" suits सहस्वतः (*sahasvataḥ*) properly, the meaning that जातूस्थिरस्य (*jātūsthirasya*) denotes a man of that name is the fitting one.

या चकर्थ सः इंद्र विश्वा असि उक्तः (*yā cakartha saḥ iṃdra viśvā asi uktaḥ*) — O Indra, because of the daring deeds of the kind mentioned above that you have done, you are praiseworthy; that is, people praise you for the deeds of daring you have done. This is the main purport.

### Printed p. 713

*Running head: Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 6, Varga 12; Ṛgveda-saṃhitā; p. 713.*

#### Ṛk 12

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> अर॑मयः॒ सर॑पस॒स्तरा॑य॒ कं तु॒र्वीत॑ये च व॒य्या॑य च स्तु॒तिं ।
> नी॒चा संत॒मुद॑नयः परा॒वृजं॒ प्रान्थं श्रो॒णं श्र॒वय॒न्तास्यु॒क्थैः॑ ॥ १२ ॥

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> अरमयः । सरऽपसः । तराय । कं । तुर्वीतये । च । वय्याय । च । स्तुतिं ।
> नीचा । संतं । उत् । अनयः । परावृजं । प्र । अंधं । श्रोणं । श्रवयन् । सः ।
> असि । उक्त्यः ॥ १२ ॥

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> हे इंद्र सरपसः! सरणमसः कर्म यासां ताः सरपसः ॥ शंकध्वादित्वात्पर-
> रूपत्वं ॥ ता अपः कं सुखेन तराय तरणायारमयः । अक्रीडयः । किंच तुर्वि-
> तये । तुर्वितिर्नाम कश्चिद्राजर्षिः । तस्मै वय्याय च । वय्यो नाम कश्चित् तस्मै ।
> ताभ्यां स्तुतिं सरणं प्रत्यरमयः । तौ हि जलपूर्णां महानदीं दृष्ट्वा तरीतु-
> मसमर्थावास्तां । तौ च त्वया तारित् । परावृजं । परितः पापानि वृणक्ति दहतीति
> परावृक् कश्चिदृषिः । तमप्पु मग्नं तथा नीचा नीचं संतमुदनयः । आपद्भ
> ऊर्ध्वं नीतवानसि । किंच अंधं संतं श्रोणं पंगुं संतं चक्षुर्दानादपंगु-
> करणाच्चोदनयः । किं कुर्वन् । प्रकर्षण श्रवयन् । आत्मानं कीर्तिमंतं
> कुर्वन् । उदनय इति समन्वयः । स इत्यादि सिद्धं ॥

*Gist: Indra made the flowing waters easy to cross for Turviti and Vayya, and raised the fallen, blind and lame Parāvṛj from distress; he is thus praiseworthy.*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

(Indra — O Indra) तुर्वीतये (*turvītaye*) — for the royal sage Turviti; वय्याय च (*vayyāya ca*) — and for Vayya; सरससः (*sarasasaḥ*) — the flowing rivers; कं (*kaṃ*) — comfortably; तराय (*tarāya*) — for crossing; स्रुतिं (*srutiṃ*) — a path; अरमयः (*aramayaḥ*) — you made; प्र श्रवयन् (*pra śravayan*) — making your fame shine; नीचा (*nīcā*) — below; संतं (*saṃtaṃ*) — who was fallen; अंधं (*aṃdhaṃ*) — who was blind; शोणं (*śoṇaṃ*) — who was lame; परावृजं (*parāvṛjaṃ*) — Parāvṛk by name; उदनयः (*udanayaḥ*) — you saved from calamity and lifted up; सः (*saḥ*) — such a you; उक्ष्यः (*ukṣyaḥ*) — worthy of praise; असि (*asi*) — you are.

### Printed p. 714

*Running head: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā; Maṇḍala 2, Adhyāya 2, Sūkta 13; p. 714.*

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O Indra, you made a path for the royal sage Turviti and for Vayya to cross the flowing rivers comfortably. Making your fame shine, you saved from calamity and lifted up Parāvṛk, who had fallen below, and was blind and lame. Such a you are worthy of praise.

**Printed English translation of Ṛk 12**

You have provided a passage for the easy crossing of the flowing waters for Turviti and for Vayya: rendering(yourself) renowned, you have uplifted the blind and lame Paravrij from the lowliness(of affliction); you are he who is to be praised.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

अरमयः (*aramayaḥ*) — अक्रीडयः (*akrīḍayaḥ*) (you caused to play). Although the root रमु क्रीडायां (*ramu krīḍāyāṃ*) means "to sport, to play", here the meaning "you made, you constructed" can be given.

सरपसः (*sarapasaḥ*) — the Pada-pāṭha authors have divided this word as सरअपसः (*saraapasaḥ*), that is, the two words सर (*sara*) and अपसः (*apasaḥ*) combined should give सरापसः (*sarāpasaḥ*); for the convenience of the metre the long vowel has been shortened to give सरपसः (*sarapasaḥ*). Sāyaṇa explains the word as सरणमपः कर्म यासां ताः सरपसः (*saraṇamapaḥ karma yāsāṃ tāḥ sarapasaḥ*), that is, rivers whose action is to move or flow, whose nature is to flow on.

The commentator's Sanskrit passage, which repeats his bhāṣya on the words Turviti, Vayya and स्तुतिं अरमयः (*stutiṃ aramayaḥ*), is quoted here. Its sense: O Indra, you prepared a way for Turviti and Vayya to cross comfortably the river flowing full with its flood. Turviti is a royal sage; Vayya is a man; when the two, unable to cross the river brimming with floodwater, were in distress, you took them across; this is the commentator's explanation of the sentence.

तुर्वीतये, वय्यायॆ (*turvītaye, vayyāyè*) — an account of Turviti and Vayya is necessary here. In the present Ṛk the commentator says that Turviti is a royal sage, and Vayya is a ... (the page, and this window, ends here in the supplied text, in mid-sentence at वय्यनॆंबु (*vayyanèṃbu*)).

### Printed p. 715

*Running head: Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 6, Varga 12; Ṛgveda-saṃhitā; p. 715.*

(Special Topics of Ṛk 12, continued from the previous page.) ...Vayya is a man, they say. But in Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-54-6 the commentator says of Vayya and Turviti: वय्यकुलजं तुर्वीतिनामानं राजानं (*vayyakulajaṃ turvītināmānaṃ rājānaṃ*) — the king named Turviti, born in the family of Vayya. Some say that Turviti was the son of Vayya. It is said that the Aśvin deities protected this Vayya and one Karkandhu, in the Ṛk

याभिः कर्कंधुं वय्यं च जिन्वथस्ताभिरू षु ऊतिभिरश्विना गतं (*yābhiḥ karkaṃdhuṃ vayyaṃ ca jinvathastābhirū ṣu ūtibhiraśvinā gataṃ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-112-6).

Concerning these two, Skandasvāmin in his Ṛgveda commentary says:

कर्कंधुः वय्यश्च राजर्षि अतिकात्रौ तपस्तप्यमानौ यदृच्छया पर्यटंतावश्विन् ददृशतुः (*karkaṃdhuḥ vayyaśca rājarṣi atikātrau tapastapyamānau yadṛcchayā paryaṭaṃtāvaśvin dadṛśatuḥ*) and दृष्ट्वा च तावमृतेनाप्याययांचक्रतुरिति तदेतदिहोच्यते (*dṛṣṭvā ca tāvamṛtenāpyāyayāṃcakraturiti tadetadihocyate*) — the two royal sages Karkandhu and Vayya, practising very painful austerity and wandering in the forest, were seen by the Aśvins by chance; the Aśvins then satisfied them with the gift of ambrosia. And again, in the Ṛk

ईशानकृद्दाशुषे दशस्यन्नुर्वीतये गाधं तुर्वणिः कः (*īśānakṛddāśuṣe daśasyannurvītaye gādhaṃ turvaṇiḥ kaḥ*) (Ma. Saṃ. 1-61-11, as supplied)

it is said that Indra helped Turviti to cross the river-floods. In the Ṛk

त्वमाविथ नर्यं तुर्वशं यदुं त्वं तुर्वितिं वय्यं शतक्रतो (*tvamāvitha naryaṃ turvaśaṃ yaduṃ tvaṃ turvitiṃ vayyaṃ śatakrato*) (Ma. Saṃ. 1-54-6)

it is said that Indra protected Turviti and "Nayya" [sic, as supplied; evidently Vayya is meant]. In the Ṛk

त्वं महीमवनिं विश्वधेनां तुर्वीतये वय्याय क्षरंतीं (*tvaṃ mahīmavaniṃ viśvadhenāṃ turvītaye vayyāya kṣaraṃtīṃ*) (Ma. Saṃ. 4-19-6)

also it is said that Indra took Turviti and Vayya across a flowing river. Besides, Turviti is mentioned in the Ṛks Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-36-18 and 1-112-23, and Vayya in the Ṛks Ṛ. Saṃ. in two Ṛks, the second Maṇḍala, Sūkta 3, Ṛk 6, and the ninth Maṇḍala, Sūkta 68, Ṛk 8 (the print joins them with a colon, which the checker reads as one reference, 2-3-6-9-68-8). The scholar Ludwig holds that Turviti was king of the tribes called the Turvaśas and the Yadus, but this has no support; it can only be said that Turviti belonged to the Turvaśa group.

The commentator's passage on the words of the Ṛk begins: नीचा संतं उत् अनयः परावृजं प्र अंधं श्रोणं श्रवयॆन् (*nīcā saṃtaṃ ut anayaḥ parāvṛjaṃ pra aṃdhaṃ śroṇaṃ śravayèn*) followed by परितः पापानि वृणक्ति दहतीति परावृक् कश्चिदृषिः (*paritaḥ pāpāni vṛṇakti dahatīti parāvṛk kaścidṛṣiḥ*) (Parāvṛk is a certain sage who, all around, destroys, burns, sins) and तमप्सु मग्नं तथा नीचा नीचं संत (*tamapsu magnaṃ tathā nīcā nīcaṃ saṃta*) (the passage breaks off here at the end of the page, mid-word, and continues on the next page).

### Printed p. 716

*Running head: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā; Maṇḍala 2, Adhyāya 3 (as printed), Sūkta 13; p. 716.*

The passage continues: मुदनयः (*mudanayaḥ*) ... आपद्भ्य ऊर्ध्वं नीतवानसि (*āpadbhya ūrdhvaṃ nītavānasi*) (you have lifted him up out of calamities); किंच अंधं संतं श्रोणं पंगुं संतं चक्षुर्दानादपंगुकरणाच्चोदनयः (*kiṃca aṃdhaṃ saṃtaṃ śroṇaṃ paṃguṃ saṃtaṃ cakṣurdānādapaṃgukaraṇāccodanayaḥ*) (also, being blind and lame, you lifted him up by giving him sight and curing his lameness); किं कुर्वन् आत्मानं कीर्तिमंतं कुर्वन् (*kiṃ kurvan ātmānaṃ kīrtimaṃtaṃ kurvan*) (doing what? making yourself renowned).

Parāvṛk was a great sage. By his power he could burn up sins so that they should not gather around him; hence the name Parāvṛk. He was lame, and blind so that he could not see, and had fallen into a lower place (or a pit). He praised Indra, and Indra, pleased with his hymn, lifted him up and saved him: this is what the sage describes here. About this sage, in the Ṛk

याभिः शचीभिर्वृषणा परावृजं प्रांधं श्रोणं चक्षस एतवे कृथः (*yābhiḥ śacībhirvṛṣaṇā parāvṛjaṃ prāṃdhaṃ śroṇaṃ cakṣasa etave kṛthaḥ*) (Ma. Saṃ. 1-112-8)

it is said that the Aśvin deities, just as in the present Ṛk, saved Parāvṛja, who was blind and lame, by giving him legs and eyes. In the Ṛk

स विद्वा अपगोहं कनीनामाविर्भवन्नु दतिष्ठत् परावृक् (*sa vidvā apagohaṃ kanīnāmāvirbhavannu datiṣṭhat parāvṛk*) प्रति श्रोणः स्थाद्व्य १नगचष्ट सोमस्य ता मद इंद्रश्चकार (*prati śroṇaḥ sthādvya 1nagacaṣṭa somasya tā mada iṃdraścakāra*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-15-7)

it is said that because Indra rejoiced after drinking Soma, the lame and blind sage Parāvṛk received eyes and legs. In the Ṛk

सरत्पदा न दक्षिणा परावृज्ज ता नु मे पृशन्यो जगृभ्रे (*saratpadā na dakṣiṇā parāvṛjja tā nu me pṛśanyo jagṛbhre*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-61-8)

the word Parāvṛk occurs, but Sāyaṇa explains it as परावर्जयिता सन् (*parāvarjayitā san*) (being one who rejects). Some English scholars hold that the word in this Ṛk means the sage mentioned above, and that the Ṛk speaks of his going to the south. They state their view:

परावृज् (*parāvṛj*) is a term found in four passages of the Rigveda, in all of which it refers to a person in a forlorn condition while one of them also speaks of him as going South. Sayanas' view that the world [sic] is a proper name is most unlikely, while Grassmann's explanation of it as cripple is still less probable. Roth's interpretation of it as exile seems clearly right in the passage which refers to the परावृज् (*parāvṛj*) as going south. Zimmer accepts Roth's view for this passage, but in the others sees a reference to the child of a maiden exposed by her and in danger of being eaten by insects (वम्रि (*vamri*)). This view is supported by the fact that परावृक्त (*parāvṛkta*) seems to have the same sense and is accepted by Oldenberg. (Vedic Index of Names & Subjects by Macdonell and Keith. P. four hundred ninety-two to four hundred ninety-three)

### Printed p. 717

*Running head: Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 6, Varga 12; Ṛgveda-saṃhitā; p. 717.*

If their view is examined together with what goes before and after, one must say that they have not understood the meaning of Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-61-8. They suppose, wrongly, that the word Parāvṛj in this Ṛk denotes the sage under discussion and that he is going south, and so express doubt. Their opinion that Sāyaṇa's explanation, that the word Parāvṛk denotes the name of a sage, is itself not right, is also not acceptable.

#### Ṛk 13

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> अ॒स्मभ्यं॒ तद्व॑सो दा॒नाय॒ राधः॒ सम॑र्थयस्व ब॒हु ते॑ वस॒व्यं॑ ।
> इंद्र॒ यच्चि॒त्रं श्र॑व॒स्या अनु॒ द्यून्बृ॒हद्व॑देम वि॒दथे॑ सु॒वीराः॑ ॥ १३ ॥

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> अस्मभ्यं । तत् । वसो इति । दानाय । राधः । सं । अर्थयस्व । बहु । ते । वसव्यं ।
> इंद्र । यत् । चित्रं । श्रवस्याः । अनु । द्यून् । बृहत् । वदेम । विदथे । सुवीराः ॥ १३ ॥

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> वसो सर्वस्य वासक वसुमन्वा हे इंद्र स्तोतृभ्योऽस्मभ्यं तद्राधो धनं
> दानाय । उपलक्षणमेतत् । भोगाय च समर्थयस्व । देहि । अस्मान् संगम-
> येत्यर्थः ॥ अर्थ याचने चुरादिरदंत आत्मनेपदी ॥ ते तव तद्बहु प्रभूतं
> वसव्यं ॥ वस्वेव वसव्यं । वस्वादित्वात् स्वार्थिको यत् ॥ तादृशं प्रभूतं धनमस्ति
> खलु । चित्रं चायनीयं यद्धनमनु द्यून् अन्वहं ॥ कालाध्वनोरिति द्वितीया ॥
> श्रवस्याः । भोग्यमिच्छेः ॥ अंतर्णीतण्यर्थत्पादकर्मकत्वं । यथा रोदितीति । स
> त्वन्यः । द्वे ह्यत्र कर्मणी उद्देश्यकर्म च विधेयकर्मांतर्भूतं । उद्देश्य-
> कर्मणा सकर्मको भविष्यति । यथा माणवकं पुत्रीयतीति भाष्य उदाहृतं । पा.
> ३-१-८-२ । श्रवःशब्दाच्छंदसि परेच्छायां क्यच् । तदंतस्य लेट्यडागमे रूपं ॥
> सुवीराः कल्याणपुत्रपौत्राः संतो वयं विदथेऽस्मिन्यज्ञॆ बृहत् प्रभूतं शस्त्रादिकं
> वाक्यं वदेम ॥

*Gist: O Indra, grant us abundant wealth for giving and enjoyment; may we, blessed with good sons and grandsons, speak great praise at the sacrifice.*

The grammatical remarks of the commentary (the root अर्थ (*artha*) in the sense of asking, of the Curādi class, ātmanepada; वसव्यं (*vasavyaṃ*) with the suffix yat in its own sense by the rule on वस्व (*vasva*) and the like; the accusative with अनु द्यून् (*anu dyūn*); श्रवस्याः (*śravasyāḥ*) formed with kyac from श्रवः (*śravaḥ*) in the sense of desiring, with a note on the two objects, the example माणवकं पुत्रीयति (*māṇavakaṃ putrīyati*), and the reference Pā. 3-1-8-2 as printed; the Vedic subjunctive with the augment) are not explained here.

### Printed p. 718

*Running head: Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā; Maṇḍala 2, Adhyāya 2, Sūkta 13; p. 718.*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

वसो (*vaso*) (*vaso*)—wealthy; इंद्र (*iṃdra*) (*indra*)—O Indra; चित्रं (*citraṃ*) (*citraṃ*)—of many kinds and delightful; यत् (*yat*) (*yat*)—which wealth; अनु द्यून् (*anu dyūn*) (*anu dyūn*)—every day; श्रवस्याः (*śravasyāḥ*) (*śravasyāḥ*)—whether we wish to enjoy it or you wish us to enjoy it; ते (*te*) (*te*)—belonging to you, बहु (*bahu*) (*bahu*)—abundant; वसव्यं (*vasavyaṃ*) (*vasavyaṃ*)—rich in possessions (the source prints "ಅದ" after it, apparently a slip); तत् राधः (*tat rādhaḥ*) (*tat rādhaḥ*)—that wealth; अस्मभ्यं (*asmabhyaṃ*) (*asmabhyaṃ*)—to us; दानाय (*dānāya*) (*dānāya*)—for giving and also for enjoyment; समर्थयस्व (*samarthayasva*) (*samarthayasva*)—give completely; सुवीराः (*suvīrāḥ*) (*suvīrāḥ*)—we, accompanied by excellent sons; विदथे (*vidathe*) (*vidathe*)—in this sacrifice; बृहत् (*bṛhat*) (*bṛhat*)—abundant śastra and other mantras; वदेम (*vadema*) (*vadema*)—we shall recite.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O wealthy Indra, give completely, both for giving and for enjoyment, that wealth which we wish to enjoy every day and which is abundant and rich in possessions with you. Accompanied by excellent sons, we shall recite abundant śastra and other mantras at this sacrifice.

**English Translation**

Possessor of riches, exert your ability to bestow wealth upon us; for yours is great affluence: may you, Indra, be disposed to grant us exceeding abundanoe [sic] day by day, so that, blessed with worthy descendants, we may glorify you at(our) sacrifice.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

Having described Indra's heroic deeds and qualities in many ways up to now, the seer, in this Ṛk, which is the last of the sūkta, concludes by praising Indra and praying that he give wealth and the like.

वसो (*vaso*) (*vaso*)—the Sanskrit gloss says "vasu-man or vāsaka of all, O Indra": the word is explained in two ways, either "O Indra, who provides a dwelling for all" or "O wealthy Indra".

अस्मभ्यं दानाय राधः समर्थयस्व (*asmabhyaṃ dānāya rādhaḥ samarthayasva*) (*asmabhyaṃ dānāya rādhaḥ samarthayasva*)—the meaning is: give us wealth both for giving to others and for our own enjoyment.

बहु ते वसव्यं (*bahu te vasavyaṃ*) (*bahu te vasavyaṃ*)—this sentence suggests that Indra has abundant wealth and the like, and therefore that he is able to give wealth and the like to those who praise him.

### Printed p. 719

*Running head: Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 6, Varga 13; Ṛgveda-saṃhitā; p. 719.*

इंद्र यत् चित्रं श्रवस्याः अनु द्यून् (*iṃdra yat citraṃ śravasyāḥ anu dyūn*) (*indra yat citraṃ śravasyāḥ anu dyūn*)—O Indra, Indra is prayed to give us, who desire wealth, wealth and other things of many kinds every day.

बृहत् वदेम विदथे सुवीराः (*bṛhat vadema vidathe suvīrāḥ*) (*bṛhat vadema vidathe suvīrāḥ*)—the commentary says: सुवीराः कल्याणपुत्रपौत्राः संतो वयं विदथेऽस्मिन्यज्ञे बृहत् प्रभूतं शस्त्रादिकं वाक्यं वदेम (*suvīrāḥ kalyāṇaputrapautrāḥ saṃto vayaṃ vidathe 'sminyajñe bṛhat prabhūtaṃ śastrādikaṃ vākyaṃ vadema*) (*suvīrāḥ kalyāṇaputrapautrāḥ saṃto vayaṃ vidathe 'smin yajñe bṛhat prabhūtaṃ śastrādikaṃ vākyaṃ vadema*). That is: accompanied by excellent sons and grandsons and by valiant attendants, we shall recite the śastra and other mantras abundantly at this sacrifice, for your pleasure, Indra; as was said in the preceding sūktas, the seer expresses this wish at the end of this sūkta too.

*The fourteenth sūkta.*

**Introduction to the sūkta (Sanskrit, transcribed)**

> अध्वर्यवो भरतेति द्वादशर्चं तृतीयं सूक्तं गार्त्समदं त्रैष्टुभ-
> मैंद्रं । अध्वर्यवो द्वादशेत्यनुक्रांतं ॥ सूक्तविनियोगो लैंगिकः । अतिरात्रॆ
> प्रथमे पर्याये होतुः शस्त्रयाज्याध्वर्यव इत्येषा । अध्वर्यवो भरतेंद्राय
> सोममिति याज्या । आ. ६-४ । इति सूत्रितं ॥
> अनुवादवु—अध्वर्यवो भरत ऎंब ई सूक्तवु ऎरडनॆय अनुवाकदल्लि मूरनॆय
> सूक्तवु. इदरल्लि हन्नॆरडु ऋक्कुगळिरुववु. ई सूक्तक्कॆ गृत्समदनु ऋषियु; इंद्रनु देव
> तॆयु; त्रिष्टुप् छंदस्सु अनुक्रमणिकॆयल्लि अध्वर्यवो द्वादश ऎंदु मुंतागि हेळिरुवुदु.
> ई सूक्तद विनियोगवु लैंगिकवु. अतिरात्रवॆंब यागदल्लि प्रथम पर्यायदल्लि होतृवु अध्व-
> र्यवो भरत ऎंब ई सूक्तद मॊदलनॆय ऋक्कन्नु शस्त्रयाज्यामंत्रवन्नागि पठिसबेकॆंदु
> आश्वलायन शौतसूत्रद—अध्वर्यवो भरतेंद्राय सोममिति याज्या ऎंब सूत्रदिंद
> विवृतवागिरुवुदु(आ. ६-४).

*Gist:* The fourteenth sūkta, *adhvaryavo bharata*, has twelve ṛks; the third sūkta of the second anuvāka; seer Gṛtsamada, deity Indra, metre Triṣṭubh; applied in the Atirātra, first paryāya, as the Hotṛ's śastra-yājyā, as prescribed in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra (Ā. 6-4).

**Anuvāda (Kannada)**

Translation—This sūkta beginning अध्वर्यवो भरत (*adhvaryavo bharata*) (*adhvaryavo bharata*) is the third sūkta in the second anuvāka. It has twelve ṛks. Gṛtsamada is the seer of this sūkta, Indra the deity, Triṣṭubh the metre; the Anukramaṇikā says अध्वर्यवो द्वादश (*adhvaryavo dvādaśa*) (*adhvaryavo dvādaśa*) and so on. The application of this sūkta is the Liṅga (by the sense of the text). In the sacrifice called Atirātra, in the first paryāya, the Hotṛ priest is to recite the first Ṛk of this sūkta अध्वर्यवो भरत (*adhvaryavo bharata*) (*adhvaryavo bharata*) as the śastra-yājyā mantra; this is set out in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra by the sūtra अध्वर्यवो भरतेंद्राय सोममिति याज्या (*adhvaryavo bharateṃdrāya somamiti yājyā*) (*adhvaryavo bharatendrāya somam iti yājyā*) (Ā. 6-4).
